item.title: MiamI (OH) scoreboard operator gets unhinged unsportsmanlike penalty vs. Ohio
item.description: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images MiamI (OH) scoreboard operator gets unhinged unsportsmanlike penalty vs. Ohio appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Miami (Ohio) RedHawks had the opportunity to stay in the MAC title game conversation, defeat a hated rival and deliver said rival its first conference loss of the season all in one night. With so much at stake, people will use all sorts of tactics to achieve victory. The players themselves fought valiantly, earning a 34-17 win versus the Ohio Bobcats, but not everyone on their side was willing to compete honorably. While the opposition attempted a field goal in the final seconds of the first half, the Miami scoreboard operator displayed photos of field goal posts in an attempt to seemingly disorient the kicker. Brack Peacock misfired from 34 yards, but the official refused to let such shenanigans go unpunished. The RedHawks got hit with possibly the strangest penalty of all-time. “On the previous play there were depictions of the field goal uprights on the scoreboard. That is a foul for unsportsmanlike conduct,” the referee declared, per Carter Lowe. We’ve seen it all now. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) I am dying 💀💀💀 https://t.co/JkoCVHdygu pic.twitter.com/yV8zu6J0h9 — Nicole Auerbach (@NicoleAuerbach) November 11, 2026 Miami (OH) actually caught a break, as the Bobcats failed to complete a pass at the goal line and went into halftime still down 17-7. Ohio roared back in the third and actually took a lead into the fourth quarter before the RedHawks scored 20 unanswered. Perhaps the football gods decided to smite the home team for its trickery, but in the Battle of the Bricks, victory is ultimately earned. Miami (OH) will celebrate this outcome and its renewed hopes in the MAC. The scoreboard operator may have to sit through a couple of unpleasant conversations, though. Related: CFB analyst destroys Oregon for main strength being ‘logo and brand identity’ Related: Robert Griffin III urges fans not to count out Ohio State football

item.title: Sandpapergate row: 'Not going to answer that' - Usman Khawaja cancels media interviews after Pat Cummins question
item.description: Former Australia opener Usman Khawaja has reportedly called off his remaining TV and radio interviews for the promotion of his autobiography, Sabr. The move follows a tough interview in which he was questioned about his claims surrounding the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, popularly known as Sandpapergate. News Corp reported that publisher Penguin informed media outlets about the cancellations on Wednesday morning. This came after Khawaja faced questions from Sarah Ferguson on ABC's 7.30. Khawaja is reportedly concerned that his future interviews will focus mainly on the ball-tampering controversy rather than the other subjects covered in his book. During Tuesday's interview, he had already indicated that he did not want to discuss the allegations any further. "I've talked on social media about this and I've written in my book, that's my statement, that's what it is, and I'm not going to really speak on any more of it at this moment in time," he said. — TUnlimitedd (@TUnlimitedd) Khawaja refuses to answer question about Pat Cummins During his conversation with Ferguson, Khawaja was asked about Warner backing his version of events and his statement that any "lies will eventually get out". "What lies is he talking about?" she asked. "I'm not going to speak on behalf of Davey," Khawaja replied. "I've tried my best to tell my story in an open and safe environment." Khawaja said he wanted the entire team to accept responsibility for the incident rather than leave three players to face the consequences. "All I've ever wanted is for us to take accountability as a team, and I don't think that's a lot to say. I'm not asking a lot from people and I say, 'We were a part of it. That was us'. Let's just take accountability. I was here to tell my truth, what I saw, what I felt, and to stick with those three guys who were made out to be the only people who have taken it [accountability]," he said. Ferguson also asked Khawaja whether Australia captain Pat Cummins knew about the use of sandpaper. However, the former opener did not answer the question. "I'm not going to answer that." He added: "I've written what I've written in my book. I've come out and stood by those three guys and told my account of what I saw." item.content:encoded: Former Australia opener Usman Khawaja has reportedly called off his remaining TV and radio interviews for the promotion of his autobiography, Sabr. The move follows a tough interview in which he was questioned about his claims surrounding the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, popularly known as Sandpapergate. News Corp reported that publisher Penguin informed media outlets about the cancellations on Wednesday morning. This came after Khawaja faced questions from Sarah Ferguson on ABC's 7.30. Khawaja is reportedly concerned that his future interviews will focus mainly on the ball-tampering controversy rather than the other subjects covered in his book. During Tuesday's interview, he had already indicated that he did not want to discuss the allegations any further. "I've talked on social media about this and I've written in my book, that's my statement, that's what it is, and I'm not going to really speak on any more of it at this moment in time," he said. — TUnlimitedd (@TUnlimitedd) Khawaja refuses to answer question about Pat Cummins During his conversation with Ferguson, Khawaja was asked about Warner backing his version of events and his statement that any "lies will eventually get out". "What lies is he talking about?" she asked. "I'm not going to speak on behalf of Davey," Khawaja replied. "I've tried my best to tell my story in an open and safe environment." Khawaja said he wanted the entire team to accept responsibility for the incident rather than leave three players to face the consequences. "All I've ever wanted is for us to take accountability as a team, and I don't think that's a lot to say. I'm not asking a lot from people and I say, 'We were a part of it. That was us'. Let's just take accountability. I was here to tell my truth, what I saw, what I felt, and to stick with those three guys who were made out to be the only people who have taken it [accountability]," he said. Ferguson also asked Khawaja whether Australia captain Pat Cummins knew about the use of sandpaper. However, the former opener did not answer the question. "I'm not going to answer that." He added: "I've written what I've written in my book. I've come out and stood by those three guys and told my account of what I saw." Cummins, along with fellow bowlers Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon, had publicly denied knowing about the incident in 2021. What did Khawaja claim about Sandpapergate? Khawaja sparked a fresh debate on Saturday by claiming that the entire Australian team knew about the ball-tampering plan during the 2018 Test against South Africa in Cape Town. His statement is different from Cricket Australia's findings at the time, which held Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft responsible for knowing about the plan before it was carried out. He also claimed that sandpaper had been used in the previous Test in Port Elizabeth, now known as Gqeberha. "It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us," he said ahead of the release of his book. Khawaja, who retired this year after playing 88 Tests, has devoted an entire chapter of his autobiography to the scandal. What punishments did Smith, Warner and Bancroft receive? The Cape Town scandal had serious consequences for Smith, Warner and Bancroft. All three players were sent home following the incident. Smith received a 12-month ban and lost the Australia captaincy. Warner was also banned for 12 months and removed from leadership positions, while Bancroft received a nine-month suspension. Khawaja believes the outcome might have been different if the entire team had accepted responsibility. "I don't believe the whole team would have got a ban if we went in together," he said. "I think it would have been shared. It's very hard to ban the whole team." Khawaja denies making claims to boost book sales Khawaja also rejected suggestions that he had made the revelations now to attract more buyers for his autobiography. He told Ferguson that the ball-tampering issue was not part of the discussion when he signed his publishing deal in 2023. He also said his manager and publisher found out about the chapter only six months ago. "Even when I gave it to them six months ago, they were shocked because I don't really talk about this to anyone," he said. The former Australia opener also explained why he chose to share his account after retiring from international cricket. "The reason I felt more comfortable saying it now is because I don't speak for the team anymore," he said. "If I try to come out and do it while I'm still on the team, they have to look at me every day. We have to go operate as a team." Cricket Australia responds to fresh allegations Cricket Australia has responded to Khawaja's claims and defended the findings of its investigation. However, it also accepted that the inquiry was completed within a short period. "The three players who received bans after the Cape Town Test acknowledged their breaches and accepted the penalties imposed," a spokesperson told Nine newspapers. "We have acknowledged that the investigation was conducted in a short timeframe given the impending Test match and that there are varying opinions about some matters including the length of the sanctions imposed. We respect that players have different recollections of events from this time. "But we remain comfortable the investigation's findings accurately reflect the statements and evidence provided at the time." Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg has ruled out reopening the investigation.

item.title: ‘They can’t trust what’s real’: Australia’s bowlers have questions to answer after Usman Khawaja claims
item.description: The pressure is mounting on Australia’s greying bowling attack: on the field, where they were well beaten by South Africa last month; and off it, where Usman Khawaja ’s autobiography has cast an old shadow over the team. Khawaja’s claim that everyone inside the Australian dressing room knew about Sandpapergate has raked up one of the darkest moments in the team’s history. “It was all of us,” he said, ahead of the publication of his new book, Sabr . “Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us.” Steve Smith ’s line immediately after that infamous day’s play in Cape Town in 2018 was that an unspecified “leadership group” knew about the plot. Later it became a select three who took the heat: the captain Smith, vice-captain David Warner and the young player caught with sandpaper in his pocket, Cameron Bancroft , who all served bans and carried the stain on their reputations far longer. Yet that has never been entirely satisfactory. Three guys knew? Really? Not their teammates? Not the staff? Not the world-class bowlers with a rigged ball in their hand? Khawaja alleges in his book that ball-tampering went on during the previous Test match in Port Elizabeth, and that an unnamed coach discussed the sandpaper plan with Bancroft. He claims the players knew, and that one bowler even said in a huddle after a wicket: “Guys, it’s going heaps now. Just don’t do anything else to it, because it’s silly how much it’s going.” Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins have always denied prior knowledge of the sandpaper plan (Getty) Former Australian bowler Mitchell Johnson wrote in a newspaper column this week: “My gut has always told me what Khawaja is now saying. As a bowler, the ball is your main tool. It’s your baby. You check it, you shine it, you take care of it every ball, every over … The idea that a ball could be scuffed with sandpaper and the bowlers wouldn’t notice didn’t make sense to me, and to plenty of people who have played the game. What disappoints me is the thought that a whole team knew and let three players take the hit.” Khawaja is the first Australian player to break cover and speak in such clear tones, and his words were backed up by Warner. “Ussie, I throw my full support behind you,” he posted. “I thank you for what you’ve done. It’s 100 per cent accurate what you’ve said. Now everyone knows the truth.” Chadd Sayers, a bowler on the tour, also endorsed Khawaja’s account. Sayers questioned Khawaja’s timing, eight years later with a book to sell. But even before these latest revelations, there were breadcrumbs of testimony. item.content:encoded: The pressure is mounting on Australia’s greying bowling attack: on the field, where they were well beaten by South Africa last month; and off it, where Usman Khawaja ’s autobiography has cast an old shadow over the team. Khawaja’s claim that everyone inside the Australian dressing room knew about Sandpapergate has raked up one of the darkest moments in the team’s history. “It was all of us,” he said, ahead of the publication of his new book, Sabr . “Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us.” Steve Smith ’s line immediately after that infamous day’s play in Cape Town in 2018 was that an unspecified “leadership group” knew about the plot. Later it became a select three who took the heat: the captain Smith, vice-captain David Warner and the young player caught with sandpaper in his pocket, Cameron Bancroft , who all served bans and carried the stain on their reputations far longer. Yet that has never been entirely satisfactory. Three guys knew? Really? Not their teammates? Not the staff? Not the world-class bowlers with a rigged ball in their hand? Khawaja alleges in his book that ball-tampering went on during the previous Test match in Port Elizabeth, and that an unnamed coach discussed the sandpaper plan with Bancroft. He claims the players knew, and that one bowler even said in a huddle after a wicket: “Guys, it’s going heaps now. Just don’t do anything else to it, because it’s silly how much it’s going.” Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins have always denied prior knowledge of the sandpaper plan (Getty) Former Australian bowler Mitchell Johnson wrote in a newspaper column this week: “My gut has always told me what Khawaja is now saying. As a bowler, the ball is your main tool. It’s your baby. You check it, you shine it, you take care of it every ball, every over … The idea that a ball could be scuffed with sandpaper and the bowlers wouldn’t notice didn’t make sense to me, and to plenty of people who have played the game. What disappoints me is the thought that a whole team knew and let three players take the hit.” Khawaja is the first Australian player to break cover and speak in such clear tones, and his words were backed up by Warner. “Ussie, I throw my full support behind you,” he posted. “I thank you for what you’ve done. It’s 100 per cent accurate what you’ve said. Now everyone knows the truth.” Chadd Sayers, a bowler on the tour, also endorsed Khawaja’s account. Sayers questioned Khawaja’s timing, eight years later with a book to sell. But even before these latest revelations, there were breadcrumbs of testimony. Bancroft’s 2021 interview with The Guardian was most telling, when he was asked if the bowlers knew what he was doing. “Obviously what I did benefits bowlers and the awareness around that, probably, is self-explanatory.” When pressed whether he meant the bowlers knew about the tampering, Bancroft added: “Uh … yeah, look, I think, yeah, I think it’s pretty probably self-explanatory.” Cameron Bancroft is confronted by umpires on the field at Newlands (Getty) Then there were recent comments by back-up spin bowler Jon Holland, a peripheral figure in the room, who revealed how the team discussed who would “take the blame” and that Smith, Warner and Bancroft were “hung out to dry”. “Once we got back to the hotel we did sit as a group [to discuss] what had happened and who was going to take the blame,” Holland told The Australian . “To Davey’s [Warner’s] credit, from what I remember, he did put his hand up and say he would take some of the responsibility, but not all of it. To be sitting there and seeing three blokes hung out to dry when you are supposed to be part of a team was a pretty hard watch.” In the aftermath of Bancroft’s Guardian interview, which made headlines in Australia, the team’s vaunted bowling attack – Mitchell Starc , Josh Hazlewood , Pat Cummins and Nathan Lyon – issued a joint statement strenuously denying prior knowledge of the ball-tampering. “We have already answered questions many times on this issue, but we feel compelled to put the key facts on the record again: we did not know a foreign substance was taken onto the field to alter the condition of the ball until we saw the images on the big screen at Newlands,” the statement read. “We respectfully request an end to the rumour-mongering and innuendo.” Nathan Lyon was among the bowlers in Australia’s 2018 touring group (PA) Look closely at the wording, and what exactly were they denying? They said they didn’t know “a foreign substance” was taken onto the field. The Independent understands that this was almost certainly true: very few of the players or staff knew Bancroft had taken sandpaper onto the field during that particular afternoon session on day three of the third Test. But what the bowlers didn’t directly address was whether they knew the Australian team were engaging in ball-tampering at any time during that match, and indeed that series. Starc said again this week: “We weren’t aware anything was taken onto the field to be tampered with,” words in line with the statement put out in 2021. What Khawaja has claimed, and Warner has backed up, is the same message Bancroft hinted and Holland implied: that an awareness of ball-tampering in the Australian dressing room extended more widely than only Smith, Warner and Bancroft. The Independent has been told that another player, along with Khawaja, pushed for the entire team to take the blame, but they were talked down. Cummins said last month that there was nothing left to discuss. “It’s obviously a long time ago,” said the Australian captain. “All the investigations, everything was done back then, answered every question a million times. It was dealt with then. All I can say is, as a group, we’ve moved on.” But after three players were punished and pilloried while the rest carried on their careers, an inquiry is needed. Cricket Australia’s investigation was inadequate – “rushed and botched”, in Warner’s words – given Khawaja’s claim that he was never even interviewed. Cricket fans “can’t trust what’s real”, former captain Michael Clarke said this week. Fresh questions must now be asked, particularly of the bowlers who denied all. Who knew ball-tampering was going on in that series? When else was the ball tampered with? Usman Khawaja (left) with Australia’s former head coach Darren Lehmann (Getty) How much did the coaches know? Darren Lehmann was head coach during the scandal, and he tearfully resigned days later, citing abuse of his family. He has always insisted he knew nothing about the plot. Mitchell Marsh is another figure in this story. He bowled during that notorious afternoon session in Cape Town but has said very little publicly. Notably, he was not a signatory on his fellow bowlers’ joint statement. With Cummins rested, Marsh is on media duties this week as Australia’s stand-in ODI captain ahead of their white-ball series against England, and no doubt he will have to confront some of the questions that linger.

item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. Because we didn’t create success for our team this season.” Latest Ducks news Oregon makes a big leap in latest College Football Playoff rankings Dan Lanning backs expanded college football playoff to 24 teams Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham takes shot at Oregon’s $50M roster Read the original article on oregonlive.com . He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. Because we didn’t create success for our team this season.” Latest Ducks news Oregon makes a big leap in latest College Football Playoff rankings Dan Lanning backs expanded college football playoff to 24 teams Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham takes shot at Oregon’s $50M roster Read the original article on oregonlive.com . item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That’s how basketball works. “That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be,” Morant said. item.content:encoded: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That’s how basketball works. “That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be,” Morant said. The 36-year-old Holiday, who would be a more natural complement next to Lillard or Morant than they are to each other, made his own case for why the point guard rotation makes sense. “It’s about being a complete basketball player for myself,” he said, “and I think we have a lot of guys like that.” There is a long history of teams talking themselves into superstar additions that make little sense. The Los Angeles Lakers once made a conscious decision to acquire Russell Westbrook and pair him with LeBron James. Nobody made them do that! The talent and star power of a Lillard-Morant backcourt is undeniable. Still, I remain unconvinced that Cronin, with a very hands-on new owner in his ear, made the deal with winning basketball games at the front of mind. Although, admittedly, Cronin’s biggest wins as a GM have been in the trade market. The haul of assets he collected for Lillard, only to get him back two years later, will go down as an all-time great swindle. So, too, will the oft-questioned Avdija trade a year later. Maybe he sees something in a Lillard-Morant pairing that many of us can’t. Morant could return to the All-Star form he had achieved before injuries and off-court issues derailed his ascent . And if he does, the Blazers can either trade him for pieces that fit better or clear out the logjam and build around him. But to sell the current roster as a basketball strategy doesn’t quite pass the smell test. Neither Lillard nor Morant has achieved stardom due to his defensive acumen. Each player needs the ball in his hands to thrive. If the duo is on the floor together, Avdija is no longer the secondary playmaker, he becomes tertiary. So, you are left to wonder whether the Blazers sold themselves on Morant because of how he can help the current collection of talent or if they simply saw the opportunity to land a 27-year-old All-NBA talent for cheap, regardless of what it meant for the existing roster construction. And if you’re being honest, you probably don’t need to wonder which of the two it is. “We were very focused and we’ll continue to be on … adding to our talent base as much as we can,” Cronin said. That thinking right there may tell you just how far ahead of everyone else the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder are in the Western Conference. They are positioned to dominate for the next half-decade, if not longer. The only chance any other team has of disrupting that is taking bold risks. But I thought the goal was to go all in on the twilight years of Lillard’s career? “Dame literally just wants to win,” said first-year head coach Micah Nori, whose charge is to sort out arguably the most talented glut of point guard talent in NBA history. “I think that’s the only thing left he really has to (do). He’s already proven he’s a winner, but at the highest level.” Does adding Morant move Lillard closer to a title? Or simply give Portland a potential off-ramp if Lillard is no longer the same player after tearing his Achilles tendon? Morant was without question a low-risk, high-reward addition. He came at the reasonable price of Jerami Grant and Kris Murray. If it becomes clear that Morant is one point guard too many, or that he’s just not the player he once was, some will argue that it didn’t cost the Blazers much to try. However, there is an opportunity cost to messing with Lillard’s swan song. If you don’t get it right, you risk wasting the gift of his voluntary return last summer . And, not for nothing, Lillard has the option to become a free agent again after this season. The franchise icon certainly hasn’t said anything that would suggest he is unhappy about Morant’s presence, although he stopped short on Monday of a full-throated endorsement. He said he knew about the trade before it went through. When I asked if he thought it was a good idea right away or if he needed time to get on board with the plan, Lillard said, “My position on it was, I’m prepared for whatever.” It’s good that he’s already thinking about other positions. Because his old one is getting awfully crowded. Read the original article on oregonlive.com . Add oregonlive.com as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

item.title: Former Real Madrid academy graduate addresses potential return and names favourite Los Blancos stars
item.description: Former Real Madrid academy graduate addresses potential return and names favourite Los Blancos stars Real Madrid have been keeping a close eye on the development of academy graduate Jacobo Ramon at Como. The young defender moved to the Italian club and has since established himself as one of the most important cogs in Cesc Fabregas’ project. He and fellow Castilla graduate Nico Paz have become two of Como’s most sought-after players. Speaking in an interview with Diario AS , Ramon discussed his future, his Madrid connections and the players who inspired him growing up. Jacobo Ramon responds to Real Madrid return rumours Asked whether he was considering a return to the Santiago Bernabeu , the defender insisted that his immediate priority was continuing his development in Italy. “I’m not thinking about it at all,” Ramon explained, pointing out that the season was still in its early stages. The youngster revealed that he had left Los Blancos specifically to get regular first-team minutes, and that the move has worked out well so far. Jacobo Ramon has performed exceedingly well at Como. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images) His performances have caught the attention of Luis de la Fuente, who has handed him a first-team call-up. Ramon also spoke about how Como had helped him improve defensively, revealing that he had gained 6 kg of muscle. Interestingly, Ramon also admitted that he would welcome the opportunity to face his former club in Europe. “I’d sign up for a Champions League semi-final against Madrid!” he declared. Ramon reveals admiration for Real Madrid legends The 21-year-old also discussed the defenders who have influenced his playing style and those he admires today. He singled out former captain Sergio Ramos for praise. “He’s my role model. I watched him the most when I was little,” Ramon explained, expressing his admiration for the legendary defender. Will Jacobo Ramon return to Los Blancos in the upcoming season? (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Interestingly, he identified Eder Militao as his favourite current player, while also praising David Alaba for looking after him during his time at Madrid. “My favourite current player is Eder Militao,” he concluded. For Los Blancos , buying back Ramon remains an exciting possibility due to a favourable clause worth around €9-10 million . However, Ramon will also know that returning to the Spanish capital might not be beneficial at this stage of his career. It remains to be seen how the 21-year-old’s career at Como progresses and whether he returns to Los Blancos in the near future.

item.title: Westlake, Georgetown and Wimberley join Lake Travis in UIL volleyball state semifinals
item.description: Westlake's Clayton Kelly (7) hits the ball as Westlake and Vandegrift face off Vendegrift in Austin, Tuesday, Aug. 18, 2026. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) Four Central Texas high school volleyball teams have made the state's UIL final four as Westlake, Lake Travis , Georgetown and Wimberley all captured regional volleyball championships Tuesday night to advance to this weekend's state semifinals. Westlake sweeps into semis Westlake setters Kyrksen Cook and Ellie Ogden combined for 35 assists as the Chaps put on a volleyball clinic of balance, ball control and teamwork to sweep San Antonio Brandeis 25-12, 25-22, 28-26 in their Region IV-6A DII final at New Braunfels Canyon. Cook had 18 assists, Ogden had 17 and two aces and Clayton Kelly had 12 kills, 18 digs and two aces. MORE: 50 Central Texas volleyball players who have had breakout seasons RELATED: UIL playoff schedule for Central Texas football teams Freshman Caroline Ehrlich and sophomore Geralynn Byers-Veal had eight kills each, and Byers-Veal served an ace on match point. Kaitlyn Tse had two aces herself as did Sunny McWilliams, who led the Chaps with 21 digs. Annabel McDuffee had three blocks. Lake Travis celebrates defeating Round Rock in the state volleyball playoffs at Burger Activity Center in Austin on Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026. Lake Travis won 3-2. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) Westlake coach Miguel Saenz has kept his team focused on the playoffs as the Chaps survived a brutal schedule and multiple injuries but still finished as tri-champions in District 25-6A with Round Rock and Lake Travis, which met Tuesday in the Region IV-6A DI final at Burger Center. The Cavaliers prevailed in five sets. "We have prepared for the playoffs since the first day of practice, to play better from day one and play hard to the finish," Saenz said. Westlake will play Katy Tompkins in Saturday's state semifinals. Georgetown lights up Tigers Georgetown dominated College Station 25-21, 25-20, 25-18 to win the Region III-5A DI championship at Giddings. Florida-bound Amelia Albright notched eight kills, had 13 digs, chalked up 28 assists and had four solo blocks to lead the Eagles into the state semifinals. Georgetown hit over .300 as a team and had nine aces. "Our serve and pass were good, and having a spread-out offense always makes winning easier," Georgetown coach Jenny Richardson said. "We had multiple hitters in a balanced offense." Claire Berryman added 11 kills, Taylor Vett had eight and Madelyn Bradley had seven. Jordan Pitkethley led the defense with 19 digs while Mallory Miller served three aces and had 10 digs. Glenn falls in five sets The Glenn Grizzlies fell in five sets after rallying from a 2-0 deficit before falling 15-12 in the final set in the Region III-5A DII final. Lake Creek's 25-15, 25-21, 25-27, 21-25, 15-12 victory sends it to the state semifinals while Glenn capped its best season in program history. item.title: ‘Par For The Course,’ ‘Stop Playing the Victim’ — Crissy Froyd Rips Dianna Russini’s Approach to Fallout From Mike Vrabel Scandal
item.description: ‘Par For The Course,’ ‘Stop Playing the Victim’ — Crissy Froyd Rips Dianna Russini’s Approach to Fallout From Mike Vrabel Scandal Former NFL insider Dianna Russini is back in sports media after a hiatus of nearly seven months. This week, Russini announced that she would be launching her own show and taking a different approach to her coverage. On Tuesday, she began sharing updates and news just hours before the official NFL trade deadline, but her attempt at seamlessly easing back into the world of NFL reporting didn’t go unnoticed, with critics like former USA TODAY reporter Crissy Froyd using the opportunity to demand accountability. Crissy Froyd Calls Out Dianna Russini Russini resigned from The Athletic in April after photographs of her with New England Patriots head coach Vrabel surfaced. A September investigation concluded that her failure to disclose the relationship violated the publication’s standards, although the review did not determine whether the relationship was romantic or find clear evidence that her reporting benefited Vrabel. In an exclusive with People , Russini opened up about her current situation and what she had been doing over the past seven months. She said she was not afraid to return, as she felt the NFL community was welcoming her back with open arms. She also emphasized that daily encouragement from players, coaches, and executives motivated her to launch her new weekly show, “The Russini Report,” on BetUS TV. As one of her first moves since announcing her comeback, Russini shared a post on X hours before Kirk Cousins was traded to the Minnesota Vikings. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator “Minnesota is calling around on QBs all day. The Vikings checked in on Mac Jones in San Francisco, but the price is too high right now. The name everyone keeps coming back to is Kirk Cousins, as Adam Schefter said. That’s the deal league sources think they’re really trying to get done,” she wrote. Froyd, who took notice of the post, quickly reacted, saying Russini cannot play the “victim” and needs to apologize. “Regurgitating news everyone already knew without any apology or recognition of wrongdoing? Par for the course. Stop playing the victim and pretending like you didn’t do exactly what you did,” she wrote on X . PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor While Russini declined to share further details about the controversy during her interview with People, she acknowledged that she planned to take a different approach to her coverage. “The way I’m going to approach stories is going to be very different now. I have an understanding and an empathy that I didn’t have before,” she said in the interview. “The Russini Report” will be a one-hour show airing every Wednesday on BetUS TV. It will be free to watch and will not require a subscription. While the show’s exact format remains unclear, Russini is expected to work toward rebuilding her credibility in the sports media landscape. Th

item.title: Does Pickford finally face serious competition for his England place?
item.description: England head coach Thomas Tuchel used James Trafford (left) and long-time first choice Jordan Pickford (right) in the previous international break [Getty Images] When England head coach Thomas Tuchel decided to pick Leeds United goalkeeper James Trafford to face World Cup holders Spain at Wembley in the last international break, it sparked the first stirrings about preparations for life without long-time first choice Jordan Pickford. Tuchel made it clear Pickford was still England's number one pick, but the simple fact he decided to alternate keepers - playing Trafford in the 3-2 loss to Spain then victory against Czech Republic, before Everton's 32-year-old returned for the Wembley win against the Czechs and the 7-0 rout in Croatia - created intrigue and debate. England meet Croatia at Wembley on Thursday before facing the biggest test of their Uefa Nations League campaign when the play Spain in Madrid on Sunday. Tuchel maintains strong faith in Pickford, an outstanding performer for England, but Trafford has at least had the chance to stake his claim. Tuchel has suggested he may use a rotation system for the pair once more in the upcoming internationals, which will only increase scrutiny on England's goalkeeping position. 'Pickford has to be at the top of his game' Pickford's record is outstanding since he made his debut in a 0-0 draw against Germany at Wembley in 2017. In his time as first choice, England have once more emerged as major players on global stage, reaching the World Cup semi-finals in 2018 and 2026, as well as successive Euros finals at the delayed 2020 tournament and Euro 2024. Measured by Opta stats, Pickford has made only two errors leading to goals in 93 appearances, with 46 clean sheets and a 74% save ratio. Trafford's international career is in its infancy and, while former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson says Pickford remains Tuchel's undisputed first choice, he believes the head coach's recent strategy is a sensible one. Robinson told BBC Sport: "It obviously remains to be seen what Thomas Tuchel does in these two England games, but I could see exactly what he was doing by giving James Trafford game time in the last round of matches. "We are so guilty as a nation of taking one goalkeeper to a tournament who has 70, 80, 90 caps, then the two of three below him could have less than double figures combined." Robinson's point is proved by the statistic that 80 of Pickford's appearances have been competitive games, with 33 at major tournaments, made up of 19 at the World Cup and 14 at European Championships. "Competitive and tournament caps give you the type of experience you can't get as a number two or three keeper," said Robinson. "James Trafford is only 24 and has four caps - two of them competitive - so you can see exactly what Tuchel is doing, looking ahead to a situation where England's recognised number one is not available to him, or there is a drop off in form. "We saw the last selections and all thought Jordan Pick
item.content:encoded: England head coach Thomas Tuchel used James Trafford (left) and long-time first choice Jordan Pickford (right) in the previous international break [Getty Images] When England head coach Thomas Tuchel decided to pick Leeds United goalkeeper James Trafford to face World Cup holders Spain at Wembley in the last international break, it sparked the first stirrings about preparations for life without long-time first choice Jordan Pickford. Tuchel made it clear Pickford was still England's number one pick, but the simple fact he decided to alternate keepers - playing Trafford in the 3-2 loss to Spain then victory against Czech Republic, before Everton's 32-year-old returned for the Wembley win against the Czechs and the 7-0 rout in Croatia - created intrigue and debate. England meet Croatia at Wembley on Thursday before facing the biggest test of their Uefa Nations League campaign when the play Spain in Madrid on Sunday. Tuchel maintains strong faith in Pickford, an outstanding performer for England, but Trafford has at least had the chance to stake his claim. Tuchel has suggested he may use a rotation system for the pair once more in the upcoming internationals, which will only increase scrutiny on England's goalkeeping position. 'Pickford has to be at the top of his game' Pickford's record is outstanding since he made his debut in a 0-0 draw against Germany at Wembley in 2017. In his time as first choice, England have once more emerged as major players on global stage, reaching the World Cup semi-finals in 2018 and 2026, as well as successive Euros finals at the delayed 2020 tournament and Euro 2024. Measured by Opta stats, Pickford has made only two errors leading to goals in 93 appearances, with 46 clean sheets and a 74% save ratio. Trafford's international career is in its infancy and, while former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson says Pickford remains Tuchel's undisputed first choice, he believes the head coach's recent strategy is a sensible one. Robinson told BBC Sport: "It obviously remains to be seen what Thomas Tuchel does in these two England games, but I could see exactly what he was doing by giving James Trafford game time in the last round of matches. "We are so guilty as a nation of taking one goalkeeper to a tournament who has 70, 80, 90 caps, then the two of three below him could have less than double figures combined." Robinson's point is proved by the statistic that 80 of Pickford's appearances have been competitive games, with 33 at major tournaments, made up of 19 at the World Cup and 14 at European Championships. "Competitive and tournament caps give you the type of experience you can't get as a number two or three keeper," said Robinson. "James Trafford is only 24 and has four caps - two of them competitive - so you can see exactly what Tuchel is doing, looking ahead to a situation where England's recognised number one is not available to him, or there is a drop off in form. "We saw the last selections and all thought Jordan Pickford's place is under threat and James Trafford is going to be the next number one. I don't think Thomas Tuchel saw it as starkly or simply as that. "It's a conversation that will definitely take place down the road, but not now. Jordan is England's first choice, in my opinion, rightfully so given his consistency and performances over such a long period. "This is a debate and conversation for the future definitely because Father Time catches up with everyone eventually and the manager needs to have a contingency plan, but Jordan Pickford very much remains number one and Thomas Tuchel has said as much. "I don't think Jordan Pickford is under threat for his jersey on a permanent basis any time soon, irrespective of the next selection, but what Tuchel is doing reinforces the impression that he has to be at the top of his game and maintain high standards, which he certainly has been doing when I've watched him this season. "The biggest compliment I can pay Jordan Pickford is that when you have got that England goalkeeper's shirt, everybody thinks somebody else should be doing it. I know that from personal experience. "You're there to be shot at, but there has been no noise around Jordan Pickford for a very long time now. "It has worked both ways for Jordan, James and Thomas Tuchel, and worked very well. Jordan knows he can't rest on his laurels and he will just play regardless. He has to be playing well. "Is James Trafford challenging Jordan Pickford right now? Yes he is - if Jordan Pickford isn't playing very well and Jordan Pickford is making errors. "None of the above are true right now because he's playing well for Everton and has done nothing wrong for England." Robinson also drew on club form to support Pickford's case. Since the start of the 2024-25 season, only Arsenal's title-winning keeper David Raya has more clean sheets in the league than Pickford at Everton. Raya has 39 clean sheets in that time, while Pickford has 27, with Robinson saying: "That's a superb record and all logic tells you Pickford will have to work a lot harder for his clean sheets than David Raya." Who are Pickford's main competitors? Trafford staked his claim in those Nations League games against Spain and the Czech Republic, putting him at the forefront of Tuchel's thoughts as the main understudy to Pickford. Crystal Palace's Dean Henderson is now back in contention after injury and hoping to add to his six caps, although he has not been included in Tuchel's latest squad. Trafford moved to Leeds United from Manchester City in the summer in a British record deal for a goalkeeper that could be worth up to £45m. It came after a £23m move to City from Burnley the previous summer, when his hopes of becoming Pep Guardiola's first choice were unexpectedly ended by the decision to sign Gianluigi Donnarumma from Paris St-Germain. Robinson said: "James Trafford needed that move to Leeds United and Leeds United needed a keeper of his level. This is a match made in heaven. "And don't forget, in a Premier League career with Burnley, Manchester City and Leeds United, Trafford has only played 42 Premier League games – just a little more than a full season – and one Champions League game. He needs this experience. "He's got a huge amount of potential, with his quality, all-round goalkeeping and mental approach. He has the potential be England's future number one, which Tuchel clearly sees him to be. "He has the mentality to reach the very top, which is very difficult because not all goalkeepers have that. It's a tough place to be, a very lonely place to be, but he has the ability to cope with that situation. "I was at Bournemouth when he made an error in the Leeds United defeat there, but, knowing the type of character he, is it won't faze him. It won't bother him. Because of his personality and his character traits, he has got the ability to go right to the top. "You'd think Dean Henderson will be back in the squad in due course once he has played more games. "Jason Steele is in there again, but he's a mentor figure behind the scenes, not someone who will ever start or threaten the established goalkeepers. "If you rewind back 18 or 24 months, you had Nick Pope, Sam Johnstone, James Trafford, Dean Henderson, Aaron Ramsdale and Jordan Pickford - a real plethora of England goalkeepers. "Now Nick Pope is not playing at Newcastle United, Sam Johnstone's not in the equation and Aaron Ramsdale is nowhere near." Ramsdale's decline has been dramatic after leaving Arsenal for Southampton in August 2024, with a loan spell at Newcastle United proving to be unsuccessful. He has effectively been fourth choice at Saints this season, failing to make matchday squads. Robinson said: "I find Aaron Ramsdale's situation very sad because I believe he's a goalkeeper able to play at the top level. "He should be in this conversation because he's a goalkeeper I really like, but he's been very unfortunate with selection of clubs an

item.title: Michael Carrick on the brink! Man Utd board set for emergency meeting with Sir Jim Ratcliffe to decide manager's fate
item.description: 마이클 캐릭 (Michael Carrick) - Getty Images Manchester United executives are meeting with Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco to determine Michael Carrick's future following a disastrous start to the season. The head coach faces the axe before the international break ends as the club languishes in the relegation zone. Man Utd chiefs discuss Carrick's future United executives are meeting with minority owner Ratcliffe this week to discuss Michael Carrick's future as head coach, as per ESPN . The 45-year-old manager is on the brink of the sack after overseeing a truly miserable start to the campaign. His struggling squad have managed just one league win so far and currently sit firmly in the Premier League's relegation places. While club sources insist a final decision has not yet been taken, Carrick is increasingly likely to lose his job in the coming days. Monaco meeting planned before Villa draw CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox will join Ratcliffe for the high-level talks in Monaco. The crucial meeting was pre-planned and not called purely in response to Sunday's chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa . However, Carrick's uncertain position is now expected to completely dominate the entire agenda. Berrada and Wilcox already discussed the developing situation during preliminary internal talks on Monday. Despite the intense speculation surrounding his job, Carrick and his backroom staff returned to the Carrington training ground on Tuesday morning. He is carrying on as normal while the majority of his squad travel away on international duty with their respective nations. Pochettino and out-of-work trio targeted If Ratcliffe backs a recommendation from Berrada and Wilcox to replace Carrick, the club have formulated a strong shortlist of established names. Mauricio Pochettino, Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte are all firmly in the frame to take over at Old Trafford. Howe, Nagelsmann and Conte are all currently out of work, making them highly accessible options for the United board. Former Ipswich Town manager Kieran McKenna also retains internal admirers after being interviewed for the managerial role earlier in 2024. However, United's dire Premier League predicament means they are highly unlikely to target a young, up-and-coming coach to lead a relegation fight. Pochettino clause opens door before Liverpool Pochettino presents a particularly intriguing option for the Red Devils hierarchy. The 54-year-old manager signed a contract extension with the USMNT in August, but his deal reportedly includes a specific clause allowing him to speak with specified European club teams. It is understood the former Tottenham boss would be extremely interested if the Old Trafford vacancy officially opens up. Time is now ticking for the United board to finalise their monumental next move. If Carrick is dismissed, the change is expected to happen before United return to action after the current international break. They face a daunting trip to Anfi

Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After a bright start to the season that saw the Wizards move above .500 for the first time in 1,423 days, malaise has started to creep into Washington's ranks. It was always fanciful to think Brian Keefe's side would scale to the top of the Eastern Conference in its first year of relevancy since the years of John Wall and Bradley Beal. Still, losses in four-straight games suggest that changes should be on the horizon in the nation's capital, even if the personnel doesn't quite accommodate for it. A.J. Dybantsa, Anthony Davis and Kyshawn George have all enjoyed strong starts to the campaign. Beyond that trifecta exists a lot of uncertainty. Will Trae Young find his shot? Will Bilal Coulibaly ever discover his? Can Alex Sarr break out of his early-year rut? These questions, and many more, will swirl as the Wizards ready for their next test, a road clash against the Pacers . Like Keefe's squad, Indiana has floundered as of late, struggling to find consistency following Tyrese Haliburton's hamstring injury. That might make the contest an ideal one for a Wizards team that needs to stop the rot sooner or later. With that, here's everything you need to know about Wizards vs. Pacers, including broadcast information and streaming options for Wednesday night's duel. item.title: The Hoddle of Coffee: Tottenham Hotspur News and Links for Wednesday, November 11
item.description: LEEDS, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 7: Archie Gray of Tottenham Hotspur during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Leeds United and Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road on November 7, 2026 in Leeds, United Kingdom. (Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images) | Getty Images good morning everyone – Some sad news out this week for Television. Richard Lloyd, the guitarist who led the cerebral dual-guitar approach with Tom Verlaine, has died. He was 75. According to a family statement, Lloyd died of a bile duct cancer called cholangiocarcinoma. There aren’t many bands out there whose sound have been as foundational to me over the last decade as Television. They were unlike anything to come out of the CBGB era. Sure they rose to power in New York City alongside the New York Dolls and Lou Reed, but they sounded as if they belonged in a Matisse, not Max’s Kansas City. It feels like you can only listen to Television at night, where you’re closer to your dreams. That’s when the music sucks you in an takes you away. Sometimes I don’t know where to start, but thankfully the options are limited. Television only released two of them, after all, and neither charted much commercial success. But where did Television fit, after all? Still, I always end with Marquee Moon , one of the most glorious tracks ever recorded. It might just be my favourite song of all time, in no small part to Verlaine and Lloyd ripping on the guitar. It’s as far away from the Ramones as you could get. So today we’re throwing it back to one of the first songs to be featured in the Track of the Day to celebrate the late great Richard Lloyd. Fitzie’s track of the day: Marquee Moon, by Television And now for your links: Football London : “Mikey Moore given brutally honest Tottenham loan verdict as manager doubles down” The Athletic ($$) : “Are Tottenham ‘complaining’ or just helping fans feel they are being represented?” The Independent : “Mauricio Pochettino becomes major candidate to replace Michael Carrick as Man United manager” The Guardian : “Mauricio Pochettino interested in leaving USMNT job for Manchester United” BBC : “Savage denies media work is impacting role as manager” New York Times : “Richard Lloyd, Torrential Guitarist of Television, Has Died” Paste : “Geese pay tribute to Television’s Richard Lloyd with cover of “Ain’t That Nothin’”“

item.title: Former Man United players’ charity once again abandoned by club in brutal act
item.description: Former Man United players’ charity once again abandoned by club in brutal act Manchester United’s owners have never had a reputation for looking after their own. Man United Season results 26/27 Cuts This has been particularly evident since Sir Jim Ratcliffe took over the running of the football operations. Since they have taken power, there have been numerous cost-cutting initiatives and staff cuts put into place. Former players and associations have also suffered, as seen two years ago when he cut a £40,000 donation to the AFMUP charity, which has been helping ex-United players since 1985. Another blow The Daily Mail reports that, “last week organisers were informed at the last minute that the second of its two annual dinners couldn’t be staged as usual in the Manchester Suite at Old Trafford and would have to move elsewhere.” Sir Alex Ferguson’s 40th anniversary party was being held in the Heritage Suite on Friday night, so as a result, “the AFMUP had to rely on Hotel Football – part-owned by Gary Neville and the Class of ’92 – coming to the rescue to host their event over the road 24 hours earlier.” Those connected to the association now fear that they will never be allowed to use Old Trafford again, as the club are now insisting that there needs to be a total of 400 guests, which is double what the charity can provide. “Previously, the AFMUP gave half of the £40,000 donation back to the club to hire the suite in April and September, raising additional funds through ticket sales and auctions.” Director of football Jason Wilcox gave a rare on-stage interview last September at one such event. In addition, Bryan Robson and Steve Bruce formed a double act at the main event this April. The paper also reports that the AFMUP’s official filmmaker and publicist, John Gubba, spoke about the latest setback on his Man Utd The Religion YouTube channel. He claimed, “while the red carpet is being rolled out for Fergie, the club have been brutally abandoning the former players’ association. The latest cutbacks by Sir Jim Ratcliffe have resulted in another kick in the teeth for the AFMUP. Staging their big event at the Theatre of Dreams was always a status that made the former players and their guests feel part of the football club. Being turfed out at short notice leaves a bitter taste.” Featured image Michael Steele via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Roma not expected to invest in January midfield signing
item.description: Roma not expected to invest in January midfield signing Gian Piero Gasperini’s second season as Roma coach is making Roma fans dream: 27 points after 11 games, 31 goals scored and 10 conceded. The Roman club is two points behind top-seeded Lazio and one behind Chivu’s Inter. D’Amico is studying the most effective strategy to strengthen the team for the Grugliasco-born coach, who has publicly stated he doesn’t want to sign for second place. What’s missing from the manager’s squad? Certainly a fast-paced attacking winger, the real priority of the upcoming transfer campaign. Will there be other signings? It doesn’t seem so… According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , Roma will focus solely on the winger, ignoring other positions as rumored in recent weeks. No other midfielder will be signed, so the squad will remain with four midfielders until the end of the season: Cristante, Koné, De Roon, and Pisilli. They will await Lorenzo Pellegrini’s recovery.

item.title: Steelers Get Telling Trade Deadline Explanation From ESPN Insider
item.description: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 01: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers passes the ball during the second quarter against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) Getty The Pittsburgh Steelers had an opportunity to add to a 6-2 team at the NFL trade deadline. General manager Omar Khan instead kept his draft picks, and a new report points to a bigger decision awaiting the franchise. While other AFC contenders made moves, Pittsburgh stood pat despite questions at wide receiver and in the secondary. According to ESPN, the Steelers’ approach has plenty to do with what happens after Aaron Rodgers. ESPN Reveals Steelers’ Trade Deadline Reasoning ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reported that Pittsburgh was one of only two AFC teams with at least six wins that failed to make a trade before Tuesday’s deadline. The Cincinnati Bengals were the other, although they reportedly backed out of a deal. Pryor pointed directly to the franchise’s unsettled quarterback future. “PIT has maintained that it doesn’t want to give up significant draft capital until it has a clear future QB plan,” Pryor wrote. That position matches what Pryor wrote in an earlier ESPN deadline preview . “Don’t mortgage the future for the present,” Pryor wrote, later adding that Pittsburgh’s “top priority remains finding their next franchise quarterback.” Rodgers, 42, has said this will be his final NFL season. The Steelers have Mason Rudolph, Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar behind him, but haven’t settled on a successor. Khan expressed optimism about the younger quarterbacks earlier this season. “We’re excited about the future with those guys, so glad we have them,” he said, according to Steelers.com’s Brian Batko . item.content:encoded: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 01: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers passes the ball during the second quarter against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) Getty The Pittsburgh Steelers had an opportunity to add to a 6-2 team at the NFL trade deadline. General manager Omar Khan instead kept his draft picks, and a new report points to a bigger decision awaiting the franchise. While other AFC contenders made moves, Pittsburgh stood pat despite questions at wide receiver and in the secondary. According to ESPN, the Steelers’ approach has plenty to do with what happens after Aaron Rodgers. ESPN Reveals Steelers’ Trade Deadline Reasoning ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reported that Pittsburgh was one of only two AFC teams with at least six wins that failed to make a trade before Tuesday’s deadline. The Cincinnati Bengals were the other, although they reportedly backed out of a deal. Pryor pointed directly to the franchise’s unsettled quarterback future. “PIT has maintained that it doesn’t want to give up significant draft capital until it has a clear future QB plan,” Pryor wrote. That position matches what Pryor wrote in an earlier ESPN deadline preview . “Don’t mortgage the future for the present,” Pryor wrote, later adding that Pittsburgh’s “top priority remains finding their next franchise quarterback.” Rodgers, 42, has said this will be his final NFL season. The Steelers have Mason Rudolph, Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar behind him, but haven’t settled on a successor. Khan expressed optimism about the younger quarterbacks earlier this season. “We’re excited about the future with those guys, so glad we have them,” he said, according to Steelers.com’s Brian Batko . Steelers Pass on Josh Downs and Other Receivers Pittsburgh’s decision was especially noticeable at wide receiver. Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac reported that the Steelers explored trades for Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs, Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and Tennessee Titans receiver Calvin Ridley. Downs ended up with the Kansas City Chiefs , who sent Indianapolis 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks and received a seventh-rounder along with the receiver. Pittsburgh no longer owns its 2027 fourth-round pick, having sent it to Dallas in a deal the Steelers announced in August. That deal brought back third- and sixth-round selections, leaving the Steelers with two picks in the third round. Thomas and Ridley remained with their teams. The Steelers’ need wasn’t imagined. Michael Pittman Jr. has played just three games because of a foot injury, while Roman Wilson has been out with a hand injury. Coach Mike McCarthy said Pittman is “getting close” to returning, according to an Associated Press report by Will Graves . Wilson could return later this month. Pittsburgh is counting on reinforcements already under contract rather than another trade. Steelers’ QB Future Remains a Bigger Question Khan took a similar approach last year, passing on receivers while preserving picks that could help Pittsburgh move up for a quarterback. Pittsburgh eventually added veteran help during the season, but its offense struggled in a playoff loss to Houston. There’s a possible cost to repeating that approach. The Steelers have won four straight and lead the AFC North, yet they’re entering the second half without the receiver addition that other contenders pursued. Still, preserving draft capital gives Khan more flexibility next spring. Pittsburgh already acquired another 2027 third-rounder from Dallas, and its first-round selection remains available if it decides to pursue a quarterback in the draft. For now, Mike McCarthy will have to make the playoff push with Rodgers and the receivers already on the roster. Pittsburgh protected its picks at the deadline, but that puts even more importance on getting its next quarterback decision right. item.title: Ryan Friedkin to arrive in Rome for transfer summit
item.description: Ryan Friedkin to arrive in Rome for transfer summit The main question Roma fans have been asking themselves in the last few hours is clear: how far can Gasperini’s team go with a major signing in the January transfer window? For some, the answer is simple: they can win the Scudetto. This question is fueling the thoughts of Gasperini and the Giallorossi management, starting with Tony D’Amico, who will be extremely busy meeting the manager’s demands. They’re also waiting for a signal from the Friedkins. In the coming weeks, the American ownership will be grappling with the final decisive steps for the stadium in Pietralata, UEFA’s ruling on the settlement agreement, and the January transfer window itself. Gasperini’s mission to strengthen Roma through the January transfer window will involve the Friedkins. As reported by Corriere dello Sport , Ryan Friedkin is expected in the capital in the coming days to discuss strategies for the upcoming transfer campaign. A plane is ready to take off from Houston, but it’s not out of the question that it could be carrying Corbin Friedkin. The ownership’s presence in Trigoria means they’re ready to go. Gasperini doesn’t want to waste time and needs a complete squad to maintain the team’s competitiveness.

item.title: Ravens Deadline Move All About Securing Depth
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - JANUARY 08: Desmond Ridder #4 of the Atlanta Falcons talks with Ryan Neuzil #64 prior to the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on January 08, 2023 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) Getty The Baltimore Ravens were active during Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. The Ravens secured C Ryan Neuzil from the Atlanta Falcons for G Andrew Vorhees and a sixth-round pick in the 2028 NFL Draft. The move might seem like an under-the-radar acquisition. But for Baltimore, the move screams depth. The team has already lost three centers this season. The losses of Danny Pinter, Jovaughn Gwyn, and Ethan Pocic forced the organization to acquire a replacement from the Philadelphia Eagles in Cam Jurgens. Now, Jurgens has been in this for three games. But the problem is that should Jurgens go down, or really any other lineman, the situation could leave the Ravens in a pickle. That’s why this deal makes sense. And as Daniel Popper noted in The Athletic , Neuzil offers depth, but also flexibility should anyone else go down this season. “Neuzil has been solid for the Falcons this season, and he is a fit in offensive coordinator Declan Doyle’s scheme. Standout rookie guard Vega Ioane was dealing with a knee sprain, but he returned in Week 9. Perhaps the Ravens wanted to shore up their center depth? They now have a capable answer if Jurgens gets injured. Or they can move Jurgens to guard if one of the guards, Ioane or John Simpson, suffers an injury. Vorhees did not play well in two starts this season. Having Neuzil would help prevent the Ravens from having to move Ioane back to center, which they did in an emergency earlier this year.” Popper gave the Ravens a B- for the deal. It’s not a bad bit of business, considering the circumstances. Ravens Still Have a Playoff Shot, and They Know It At 4-5, the Ravens don’t have much runway, but their playoff hopes are not exactly on life support. Baltimore still has the playoffs within reach. That’s why throwing in the towel now doesn’t make any sense. And if the organization thinks that it has a legit chance to challenge for the Super Bowl, it needs to take steps to avoid devastating issues. Hence, the offensive line is an obvious concern. Baltimore has already dealt with a revolving door at center, and another injury could leave the club in a pretty pickle. It’s also worth noting that Jurgens has only been with the team for three games, that’s why having another capable option behind him makes sense. The Ravens also need to protect their flexibility at guard rather than constantly reshuffling the line whenever someone goes down. That’s what makes Ryan Neuzil a sensible addition. Make no mistake. This isn’t a move that will suddenly transform Baltimore’s offense. But it’s the type of move that could prevent one more injury from becoming a devastating problem. At this point, the Ravens need every bit of stability they can find. If they want to stay in the playoff hunt
