(Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) Getty The Baltimore Ravens were active during Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. The Ravens secured C Ryan Neuzil from the Atlanta Falcons for G Andrew Vorhees and a sixth-round pick in the 2028 NFL Draft. The move might seem like an under-the-radar acquisition. But for Baltimore, the move screams depth. The team has already lost three centers this season. The losses of Danny Pinter, Jovaughn Gwyn, and Ethan Pocic forced the organization to acquire a replacement from the Philadelphia Eagles in Cam Jurgens. Now, Jurgens has been in this for three games. But the problem is that should Jurgens go down, or really any other lineman, the situation could leave the Ravens in a pickle. That’s why this deal makes sense. And as Daniel Popper noted in The Athletic , Neuzil offers depth, but also flexibility should anyone else go down this season. “Neuzil has been solid for the Falcons this season, and he is a fit in offensive coordinator Declan Doyle’s scheme. Standout rookie guard Vega Ioane was dealing with a knee sprain, but he returned in Week 9. Perhaps the Ravens wanted to shore up their center depth? They now have a capable answer if Jurgens gets injured. Or they can move Jurgens to guard if one of the guards, Ioane or John Simpson, suffers an injury. Vorhees did not play well in two starts this season. Having Neuzil would help prevent the Ravens from having to move Ioane back to center, which they did in an emergency earlier this year.” Popper gave the Ravens a B- for the deal. It’s not a bad bit of business, considering the circumstances. Ravens Still Have a Playoff Shot, and They Know It At 4-5, the Ravens don’t have much runway, but their playoff hopes are not exactly on life support. Baltimore still has the playoffs within reach. That’s why throwing in the towel now doesn’t make any sense. And if the organization thinks that it has a legit chance to challenge for the Super Bowl, it needs to take steps to avoid devastating issues. Hence, the offensive line is an obvious concern. Baltimore has already dealt with a revolving door at center, and another injury could leave the club in a pretty pickle. It’s also worth noting that Jurgens has only been with the team for three games, that’s why having another capable option behind him makes sense. The Ravens also need to protect their flexibility at guard rather than constantly reshuffling the line whenever someone goes down. That’s what makes Ryan Neuzil a sensible addition. Make no mistake. This isn’t a move that will suddenly transform Baltimore’s offense. But it’s the type of move that could prevent one more injury from becoming a devastating problem. At this point, the Ravens need every bit of stability they can find. If they want to stay in the playoff hunt, shoring up the offensive line is a pretty good place to start. Baltimore Got Neuzil for a Reasonable Price The other appealing part of this deal is what Baltimore actually had to give up to get Neuzil. The Falcons could have taken Baltimore to the cleaners. The Ravens’ need was clear, and it could have given Atlanta a chance to clean up. Instead, the Falcons actually did Baltimore a solid. Instead of sticking it to them, Atlanta was willing to take a much lower return than it could have otherwise gotten. What Baltimore paid was a relatively modest price for a player who gives Baltimore another legitimate option across the interior offensive line. Vorhees had struggled in his opportunities this season, making the cost easier to stomach. And while giving up a draft pick is never ideal, a late-round selection two years from now is a small price to pay for insurance at a position that has already caused the team plenty of headaches. The Ravens didn’t need to make a splash at the deadline. They needed to address a weakness before it became an even bigger problem. Neuzil gives them that protection without forcing them to surrender a premium asset. That’s the kind of practical deadline business a team still fighting for a playoff spot should be making. item.title: Kings’ Darius Acuff Jr. doesn’t hold back on 1-10 record after loss to Magic
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images Kings’ Darius Acuff Jr. doesn’t hold back on 1-10 record after loss to Magic appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Sacramento Kings are spiraling early in the season, and rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr. isn’t trying to sugarcoat the frustration anymore. Sacramento hit another low point on Tuesday night, falling 107-100 to the Orlando Magic at Golden 1 Center. The defeat dropped the Kings to a dismal 1-10 record, tying the worst 11-game start in franchise history. Despite the team’s ongoing slide, Acuff put on another spectacular individual show. The 18-year-old guard led Sacramento’s attack with 29 points, six assists, and four rebounds while playing 40 minutes. But personal box-score numbers meant very little to the rookie after watching another winnable game slip away in front of the home crowd. Following the loss, beat reporter Frankie Cartoscelli posted on X that Acuff was visibly frustrated while addressing the media. The rookie guard held nothing back when assessing Sacramento’s struggles. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “1-10 just don’t sound right,” Acuff said. “There’s nobody to blame but ourselves… We’re trying; we’re talking as a team. When the clock hits zero and we’re losing, that’s the most frustrating part.”Acuff has shouldered a massive load early, becoming the first NBA rookie since 1983 to attempt at least 20 shots in each of his first 10 career games. He got offensive support from veteran guard Zach LaVine, but Sacramento couldn’t string together enough late stops. Orlando executed key possessions down the stretch, keeping the Kings winless at home with an 0-6 mark. Sacramento’s locker room communication has yet to pay dividends on the court. While Acuff continues to show superstar potential, high-scoring nights won’t soften the blow for a rookie driven by winning. Until the Kings fix their late-game execution, the frustration in Sacramento will only build. item.title: 76ers’ Joel Embiid calls Paul George Celtics’ ‘best player’
item.description: © Bill Streicher-Imagn Images 76ers’ Joel Embiid calls Paul George Celtics’ ‘best player’ appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Philadelphia 76ers star Joel Embiid is very happy for his former teammate and Celtics veteran, Paul George. In a 123-101 loss to the Celtics, foul trouble disrupted 76ers All-Star Jaylen Brown’s rhythm against his former team. At the same time, the other player involved in their blockbuster trade over the summer — George — thrived, scoring a game-high 36 points in his first game back in Philadelphia. While fans were fixated on how the former Celtic would perform against his former team, Brown might have had his worst game since his trade. George, on the other hand, turned in his best of the young regular season, of which Embiid commended during his postgame availability, per PHLY Sports’ Derek Bodner. “Off the court we have a special relationship. Families are close, especially our kids. I love him,” Embiid said. “That’s why I’m extremely happy for him. He’s healthy, he’s playing well. The start of the season, you see what he did tonight. You can kinda say he’s been their best player on some level. So, I’m extremely happy for him. Proud of him.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joel Embiid on his relationship with Paul George : "Off the court we have a special relationship. Families are close, especially our kids. I love him. That's why I'm extremely happy for him. He's healthy, he's playing well…You can kinda say he's been their best player." pic.twitter.com/WCRUsrBO3d — Derek Bodner (@DerekBodnerNBA) November 11, 2026 Celtics’ Paul George drained six threes en route to his 36 points. He also finished with five rebounds and one assist, while Jayson Tatum tallied 21 points, six rebounds, four assists, and two blocks. 76ers’ Joel Embiid finished with 16 points, six rebounds, and one assist. Tyrese Maxey’s 24 points led Philly in scoring, while Brown added 13 points, five rebounds, two assists two steals, and one block against the Celtics. Embiid and the 76ers will look to bounce back from their 22-point loss when they host the Toronto Raptors on Thursday. item.title: Horizon League awards Wright State Raiders player with weekly honor
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - MARCH 20: TJ Burch #22 and Andrea Holden #20 of the Wright State Raiders celebrate against the Virginia Cavaliers during the second half in the first round of the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament at Xfinity Mobile Arena on March 20, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Emilee Chinn The Horizon League recognized a Wright State University men’s basketball player this week. item.title: Colts headline 3 biggest losers of 2026 NFL trade deadline after keeping Jonathan Taylor
item.description: Colts headline 3 biggest losers of 2026 NFL trade deadline after keeping Jonathan Taylor appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . And just like that, the 2026 NFL trade deadline was in the books . Suddenly, all of the rumors were either proven true or false, all of the speculation came to an end, and fans had a chance to see what their favorites will more or less look like when the playoffs roll around come January. For some teams, they made out like bandits, adding the perfect players for their schemes at a reasonable price, but for others, three teams exactly, things didn’t go exactly how they’d hoped, leaving picks on the table, overpaying for players, or simply showing a fundamental misunderstanding of the rules that resulted in a major faux pas on deadline day. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mandatory Credit: Travis Register-Imagn Images The Colts left too many picks on the table by keeping Jonathan Taylor As an entire swash of NFL teams looked to load up on the finishing touches for their Super Bowl-caliber rosters, the Colts and Eagles found themselves as the two biggest sellers in a buyer’s market and were able to load up on draft picks in exchange for win-now players. And yet, when push came to shove, the Colts removed their best chip from the table before the die was cast, losing out on “ a second-round pick and more ” for 27-year-old running back Jonathan Taylor , according to Fox Sports’ Jordan Schutlz. “Sources: The Colts had multiple offers of a 2nd-round pick and more for RB Jonathan Taylor over the last week,” Schutlz wrote. “But the organization decided that if it ever trades him, it will be in the offseason, when more buyers could be available, and a permanent GM is in place.” On paper, the idea of waiting until the offseason to trade Taylor isn’t the worst one, as there could be additional teams interested in his services, but what there won’t be is the same sense of urgency that exists at the trade deadline, where teams are willing to pay extra for that missing piece. Factor in the potential for Taylor to get injured over the final eight games, where he’s averaging 20.7 touches per game, and the Colts are making a major bet that might not cash in the way they hope. The Colts also opted against trading Grover Stewart , who is a free agent at the end of the season, and probably could have gotten way more than a third-round pick for Daniel Jones from the Minnesota Vikings if they were willing to really sell the doors off their building, which may or may not pay off, depending on how the next 12 months shake out. Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The Jaguars were rightfully blasted for Jordan Davis ’ price tag On Monday, the Jacksonville Jaguars shocked the NFL world by not only trading for Jessie Bates III and Davon Godchaux but also backing up the Brinks truck to the deadline’s other big seller, the Eagles, to take over the remainder of Jordan Davis’ long-term contract. item.content:encoded: Colts headline 3 biggest losers of 2026 NFL trade deadline after keeping Jonathan Taylor appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . And just like that, the 2026 NFL trade deadline was in the books . Suddenly, all of the rumors were either proven true or false, all of the speculation came to an end, and fans had a chance to see what their favorites will more or less look like when the playoffs roll around come January. For some teams, they made out like bandits, adding the perfect players for their schemes at a reasonable price, but for others, three teams exactly, things didn’t go exactly how they’d hoped, leaving picks on the table, overpaying for players, or simply showing a fundamental misunderstanding of the rules that resulted in a major faux pas on deadline day. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mandatory Credit: Travis Register-Imagn Images The Colts left too many picks on the table by keeping Jonathan Taylor As an entire swash of NFL teams looked to load up on the finishing touches for their Super Bowl-caliber rosters, the Colts and Eagles found themselves as the two biggest sellers in a buyer’s market and were able to load up on draft picks in exchange for win-now players. And yet, when push came to shove, the Colts removed their best chip from the table before the die was cast, losing out on “ a second-round pick and more ” for 27-year-old running back Jonathan Taylor , according to Fox Sports’ Jordan Schutlz. “Sources: The Colts had multiple offers of a 2nd-round pick and more for RB Jonathan Taylor over the last week,” Schutlz wrote. “But the organization decided that if it ever trades him, it will be in the offseason, when more buyers could be available, and a permanent GM is in place.” On paper, the idea of waiting until the offseason to trade Taylor isn’t the worst one, as there could be additional teams interested in his services, but what there won’t be is the same sense of urgency that exists at the trade deadline, where teams are willing to pay extra for that missing piece. Factor in the potential for Taylor to get injured over the final eight games, where he’s averaging 20.7 touches per game, and the Colts are making a major bet that might not cash in the way they hope. The Colts also opted against trading Grover Stewart , who is a free agent at the end of the season, and probably could have gotten way more than a third-round pick for Daniel Jones from the Minnesota Vikings if they were willing to really sell the doors off their building, which may or may not pay off, depending on how the next 12 months shake out. Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The Jaguars were rightfully blasted for Jordan Davis ’ price tag On Monday, the Jacksonville Jaguars shocked the NFL world by not only trading for Jessie Bates III and Davon Godchaux but also backing up the Brinks truck to the deadline’s other big seller, the Eagles, to take over the remainder of Jordan Davis’ long-term contract. When the news broke, Jaguars fans were rightfully excited, as they nabbed a key defensive cog from a recent Super Bowl champion to hopefully lead them to their own run at the “big game,” but as the dust settled, it rapidly looked like Howie Roseman fleeced James Gladstone out of a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-rounder for a part-time player in the middle of a down season. Need proof? Well, look no further than ESPN, where a tag team article by Ben Solak and Seth Walder gave the Jaguars an F for the deal. Why? Well, because Davis simply isn’t the kind of player worthy of that kind of return. “There’s no other way to start this: This trade is a disaster for Jacksonville,” the duo wrote. “The numbers do not paint a picture of Davis being someone who is worth anywhere near that type of trade compensation. He has played 52% of snaps for the Eagles. That number is not particularly unusual for a run-stuffing nose tackle, but that’s exactly the point: The Jaguars just dealt first- and second-round picks for a part-time player who helps only against the run! There is no world where that is worth it.” Now granted, Davis brings more to the table than just stopping the run. He’s a great locker room guy, a team leader, and one of the most athletic nose tackles the NFL has ever seen. But the Eagles simply never trusted him to rush the passer with regularity, which is a big part of playing defensive tackle in the NFL regardless of scheme, especially on a $78 million contract. Who knows, maybe the Jaguars will give Davis more of a go since they don’t also have Jalen Carter and Moro Ojomo looking for snaps, but unless he suddenly becomes a three-down player, it’s hard to argue the Jaguars didn’t pay a serious premium for a part-time player, which is all the more confusing since they added another run-stuffing defensive tackle earlier in the day. Edward Finan-Imagn Images The Bengals not knowing the compensatory draft formula rules Normally, when a team opts to trade a sixth-round pick for a rotational edge rusher, it’s pretty low on the proverbial priority list, especially when multiple first- and second-round picks were moved before the deadline. The Cincinnati Bengals ’ decision to almost trade for Eagles outside linebacker Arnold Ebiketie is the rare exception, as the reason it didn’t happen is downright goofy. Taking to social media to explain the situation for fans who don’t know the inner workings of the compensatory formula – a disproportionate number of whom may live in the Buckeye State – The Ringers’ Albert Breer revealed that had the deal gone through, Duke Tobin would have been giving up a whole lot more than a sixth-round pick . “Explaining the Arnold Ebiketie situation. The rule in question was put in years ago to close a loophole teams could exploit by executing a sign-and-trade with other teams—and basically says that if you trade for a player in the first year of his contract, he counts against the comp-pick formula as if he was a free agent you signed,” Breer wrote. “Had the Bengals gone through with this trade, they’d have gained three compensable free agents, and lost three, leaving them without a pick for Trey Hendrickson. So while on paper, they’d have gotten Ebiketie for a sixth-rounder, as a practical matter, they’d have traded him for third- and sixth-round picks (the third being the comp pick they’ll likely get for Hendrickson). That’s why the trade is off.” At the end of the day, does it really matter if the Bengals added a player like Ebiketie, who doesn’t have a sack in 2026 over 300 defensive snaps? Not really, especially since their pass rush currently ranks ninth in the NFL in terms of sacks, and players like Boye Mafe have come into their own without Trey Henderson. But not knowing how the compensatory pick formula works? Especially when Tobin has been with the team for 25 years? That certainly is not a good look for a team that has routinely been on the wrong side of personal drama. Related: Where 2026 NFL trade deadline falls in league history Related: Josh Downs trade grades for Chiefs, Colts as Patrick Mahomes gets new weapon

item.title: Liverpool prodigy Rio Ngumoha explains how Barcelona superstar has inspired young footballers: ‘He plays as if…’
item.description: Liverpool prodigy Rio Ngumoha explains how Barcelona superstar has inspired young footballers: ‘He plays as if…’ Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha has credited Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal with changing the way young footballers approach the game, describing the teenager as one of the best players in the world. Speaking in an interview with The Independent , the 18-year-old England international highlighted how Yamal’s confidence, freedom and performances at such a young age have inspired the next generation. Ngumoha’s comments come ahead of England’s November Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain. Thomas Tuchel has included the Liverpool winger in his squad following his encouraging performances at club level, potentially giving him an opportunity to face the Barcelona star when England meet Spain. Ngumoha sees Yamal as an inspiration for young players Speaking during a lengthy interview, Ngumoha did not hide his admiration when asked about the Barcelona winger, whose development has established him among the leading young talents in European football. Rio Ngumoha sees Lamine Yamal as an inspiration. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) “I think what he’s doing has changed football for young players. He’s extraordinary. He’s one of the best in the world,” said Ngumoha when asked about the Barcelona star. The Liverpool forward believes Yamal’s performances show that young footballers should not be afraid to express themselves or take responsibility on the pitch. Rather than allowing their age to restrict their ambitions, they can use his example as encouragement to play with confidence. “Seeing what he can do at such a young age inspires me and all the other young players to play freely. “He plays as if the pitch were his own. It’s a great challenge,” noted the Reds’ forward. England call-up pit Ngumoha against Yamal Rio Ngumoha could come up against Yamal later this month. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images) Ngumoha’s admiration for Yamal could soon become a personal challenge. This is because England are scheduled to face Croatia on November 12 before travelling to Spain on November 15 at the Metropolitano, with the latter fixture potentially bringing the two young wingers onto the same pitch. At 18, Ngumoha is the youngest player in Tuchel’s November England squad and has already made his senior international debut. Yamal, on the other hand, is an established member of Barcelona and Spain’s setup, and a meeting with the Spaniard would offer Ngumoha an opportunity to test himself against a player whose development he clearly admires.

item.title: Filip Forsberg scores twice as Predators blank Kings
item.description: Los Angeles Kings right wing Alex Laferriere (14) fights for the puck during their game against the Nashville Predators at Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Los Angeles. LOS ANGELES — The Los Angeles Kings entered Tuesday night seeking a bounce-back victory following Saturday’s loss to the Pittsburgh Penguins and looking to establish consistency on home ice. Instead, the club's offensive droughts resurfaced as Los Angeles was shut out for the first time this season, falling 3-0 to the Nashville Predators at Crypto.com Arena. The frustration surrounding another quiet night from the offense was evident after the game. "I think everybody’s probably frustrated," head coach Peter Laviolette said. "We’re here to win hockey games and we’re not getting that done." In a unique matchup featuring a battle of matching surnames — Nashville forward Filip Forsberg facing off against Los Angeles goaltender Anton Forsberg — the Predators' star winger got the upper hand over his counterpart, striking twice to pave the way for a Nashville road win. Coming into the contest, both clubs averaged exactly 3.00 goals per game, reflecting similar scoring metrics on paper. On Tuesday night, however, Nashville simply executed when opportunities arose while the Kings failed to convert on their own looks. "There were point blank chances and rebound chances and just not able to capitalize," Laviolette said. "I don’t think we made the plays quick enough." The Predators broke the ice midway through the opening frame off an unforced error. Nils Hoglander intercepted a pass from Kings defenseman Brian Dumoulin and led a two-on-one odd-man rush down the ice, feeding Filip Forsberg, who buried a one-timer to put Nashville ahead with 14:40 remaining in the first period. The Nashville Predators players celebrate a goal during their game against the Los Angeles Kings at Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Los Angeles. Dakota Gray - The Sporting Tribune The Nashville Predators players celebrate a goal during their game against the Los Angeles Kings at Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Los Angeles. After Los Angeles closed the first period strong and carried momentum into the middle frame, the Hoglander-to-Forsberg connection struck again. Halfway through the second period, Hoglander centered a pass to the two-time All-Star at the faceoff dot, where the 32-year-old Swede snapped a shot top-shelf for his seventh goal of the season, doubling the Predators' cushion. An empty-net tally by Adam Wilsby with under two minutes remaining slammed the door on a disappointing night for Los Angeles, dropping the club to 5-9-2 on the year and leaving the locker room searching for answers. "I think [we] didn't feel connected out there at all," winger Adrian Kempe said. "Overall, pretty disappointed." item.content:encoded: Los Angeles Kings right wing Alex Laferriere (14) fights for the puck during their game against the Nashville Predators at Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Los Angeles. LOS ANGELES — The Los Angeles Kings entered Tuesday night seeking a bounce-back victory following Saturday’s loss to the Pittsburgh Penguins and looking to establish consistency on home ice. Instead, the club's offensive droughts resurfaced as Los Angeles was shut out for the first time this season, falling 3-0 to the Nashville Predators at Crypto.com Arena. The frustration surrounding another quiet night from the offense was evident after the game. "I think everybody’s probably frustrated," head coach Peter Laviolette said. "We’re here to win hockey games and we’re not getting that done." In a unique matchup featuring a battle of matching surnames — Nashville forward Filip Forsberg facing off against Los Angeles goaltender Anton Forsberg — the Predators' star winger got the upper hand over his counterpart, striking twice to pave the way for a Nashville road win. Coming into the contest, both clubs averaged exactly 3.00 goals per game, reflecting similar scoring metrics on paper. On Tuesday night, however, Nashville simply executed when opportunities arose while the Kings failed to convert on their own looks. "There were point blank chances and rebound chances and just not able to capitalize," Laviolette said. "I don’t think we made the plays quick enough." The Predators broke the ice midway through the opening frame off an unforced error. Nils Hoglander intercepted a pass from Kings defenseman Brian Dumoulin and led a two-on-one odd-man rush down the ice, feeding Filip Forsberg, who buried a one-timer to put Nashville ahead with 14:40 remaining in the first period. The Nashville Predators players celebrate a goal during their game against the Los Angeles Kings at Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Los Angeles. Dakota Gray - The Sporting Tribune The Nashville Predators players celebrate a goal during their game against the Los Angeles Kings at Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Los Angeles. After Los Angeles closed the first period strong and carried momentum into the middle frame, the Hoglander-to-Forsberg connection struck again. Halfway through the second period, Hoglander centered a pass to the two-time All-Star at the faceoff dot, where the 32-year-old Swede snapped a shot top-shelf for his seventh goal of the season, doubling the Predators' cushion. An empty-net tally by Adam Wilsby with under two minutes remaining slammed the door on a disappointing night for Los Angeles, dropping the club to 5-9-2 on the year and leaving the locker room searching for answers. "I think [we] didn't feel connected out there at all," winger Adrian Kempe said. "Overall, pretty disappointed." While Anton Forsberg kept the Kings within striking distance, Predators goalie Juuse Saros delivered a flawless performance at the opposite end, stopping all 30 shots he faced to record his first shutout of the season. When the offense sputters, wins are hard to come by for Los Angeles. Plain and simple. In Laviolette's first season behind the bench, the Kings are 0-8-1 when scoring two goals or fewer, spotlighting a concerning trend early in the campaign. Los Angeles has struggled to extract wins from tightly contested, low-scoring games — finding success only when the offense is humming. Despite surrendering two goals to his namesake counterpart, Anton Forsberg stood tall as one of the brightest spots on the ice for Los Angeles, turning aside 27 of 29 shots. Yet when the veteran goalie gets the nod, run support remains elusive. In his six starts this season, the Kings are 0-5-1 while averaging a subpar 1.5 goals per game. "He’s played good for us," center Scott Laughton said of Forsberg’s effort. "We need to find a way to find sustained zone time in the offensive zone, wear teams down, where they’re tired and we three-quarter ice them. It’s just not happening right now." In order to climb out of their losing ways, individual accountability across the lineup will be essential moving forward. "I haven’t been good enough," Laughton said. "I need to bring more to this group and I’m sure a lot of guys would say the same." Despite the early-season adversity, the sentiment inside the locker room remains focused on constantly improving and keeping the energy high. "We're a good hockey team," Laughton said. "I believe that. We've got to have that belief in the group and we’ve got to continue to push forward here."

item.title: Carlos Espi talks Mbappe, Ballon d’Or, Mourinho and Premier League interest
item.description: Carlos Espi talks Mbappe, Ballon d’Or, Mourinho and Premier League interest There is no doubt that Kylian Mbappe is one of the best players on the planet, and his second-placed finish on the Ballon d’Or standings reflects the same. His numbers at Real Madrid are staggering, and he has already made the number nine position his own with Los Blancos . The club did, however, see the need to keep a backup player in the position and went on to bring in Carlos Espi – a player who provides a more direct goalscoring threat as a traditional number nine. So far, the duo have worked very well in tandem. While it is Mbappe who starts and hogs a massive part of the minutes, Espi has stepped up with clutch goals when Real Madrid have needed them most. Espi heaps praise on Mbappe Espi and Mbappe in action. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images) Speaking to the media on duty with the Spain U21 team, the youngster commented on Kylian Mbappe and revealed his two cents on the Frenchman’s quality. “Kylian Mbappe is the best player in the world. To me, he deserved the Ballon d’Or,” he added. He then revealed how just training with the forward taught him a lot and helped him improve. “Every training session I spend with him, I try to learn as much as I can from him, and listen to everything he tells me. “His speed, his dribbling, his goalscoring, it’s incredible to watch, really,” he added. On Jose Mourinho The manager then commented on Jose Mourinho and how the manager was transforming the dressing room into a winning machine. “José Mourinho is incredible,” he began. “He’s very close to us, very demanding, and that’s a very good thing,” he added. Espi appreciated Mourinho’s management. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) Espi then revealed how it felt personally to work with the legendary manager, and how his relationship with the coach was. “It’s great to have him so close to me, telling me what I did well and what I did badly, I’m very happy with José.” Espi speaks on his time at Real Madrid Finally, the player expressed what a privilege it was to play for Real Madrid. “To me, every minute I spend on the pitch for Real Madrid is golden.” “Every opportunity to play is a golden opportunity,” he added. He acknowledged that he was not receiving as many minutes as he liked, but also stressed that he is willing to wait for his chances. “Of course I’d like to play more, every player does, but I just focus on taking full advantage of every opportunity the coach gives me to play.” Finally, Espi revealed how he could have signed for multiple Premier League sides in the summer and how Real Madrid’s arrival on the scene changed everything. “It’s true that I could’ve gone to the Premier League last summer, but when Real Madrid called, I could not say no.” Source: Cadena SER

item.title: Jets Take Parting Shot at Connor Hellebuyck After Beating Devils
item.description: Connor Hellebuyck Jets Devils Getty The Winnipeg Jets organization took a parting shot at former goalie Connor Hellebuyck after beating the New Jersey Devils on Tuesday night. In one of the most highly anticipated games of the year, the Jets beat the Devils 4-2 on Tuesday night in Winnipeg, in Hellebuyck’s return to the city where he spent the first 11 seasons of his NHL career. Dawson Mercer, who was part of the trade package for Hellebuyck, scored twice against his former team as the Jets won their fourth straight game. Meanwhile, the Devils lost with Jake Allen in net, as the team said that starting Hellebuyck would have given the team a lower chance to win the game, something the Jets organization had a field day with after beating New Jersey. Jets Take Parting Shot at Devils On their social media, the Jets made it clear where they stood with the Devils’ decision not to start Hellebuyck against them due to analytical reasons. “Expected Win Probability 100%,” the Jets wrote on their X . Expected Win Probability 100% ✈️ @Wawanesa | #GoJetsGo pic.twitter.com/1SIWKkjSUK — Winnipeg Jets (@NHLJets) November 11, 2026 It’s a brutal message from the Jets to the Devils and their former franchise goalie, Hellebuyck, but it’s one that is deserved, as Hellebuyck gave up on his former team and demanded a trade out of Winnipeg, even deciding not to show up to training camp while awaiting a trade. Devils Look Foolish for Connor Hellebuyck Decision Ever since the Jets announced on their social media that they would be sitting Hellebuyck for this game against the Jets due to analytics, they have been the butt-end of jokes from those in the hockey world, and for good reason, as their reasoning to sit their starting goalie made zero sense. The fact that the Devils pointed to analytics as the reason they didn’t want to start Hellebuyck was laughable and made them look foolish to the entire NHL. It makes you wonder who allowed the Devils’ PR team to release such an outlandish statement, knowing what the reaction to it would be. In the end, though, the Jets got the last laugh, and the Devils look like fools for keeping Hellebuyck out of this game. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Jets Take Parting Shot at Connor Hellebuyck After Beating Devils appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: ‘Took This Personal,’ ‘True Revenge Game’ — NBA World Raves As Paul George Outshines Jaylen Brown in Celtics-76ers Clash With ‘Vintage’ 36-Point Night
item.description: 'Took This Personal,' 'True Revenge Game' — NBA World Raves As Paul George Outshines Jaylen Brown in Celtics-76ers Clash With 'Vintage' 36-Point Night Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown’s first regular-season meeting as opponents headlined Tuesday’s marquee matchup between the Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers. However, Paul George stole the show, leading all scorers with 36 points in Boston’s resounding 123-101 road win. Acquired in the surprising offseason trade that sent Brown to the 76ers, the nine-time All-Star shined in his first game back in Philadelphia. George’s vintage performance drew high praise from around the NBA world, with some contrasting it with his underwhelming, injury-plagued stint with the 76ers, which the 36-year-old addressed after the game. Paul George’s Dominant Return to Philadelphia Fuels Redemption-Season Buzz George shot 14-for-22 overall (63.6%), including 6-for-11 from 3-point range (54.5%), adding 5 rebounds and 1 assist in only 30 minutes. Boston broke a 79-79 tie with a late third-quarter run, and the veteran forward took over from there. He scored 14 consecutive Celtics points in a stretch of just under 4 minutes in the final frame, extending Boston’s lead from 97-82 to 111-87. In contrast, Brown struggled to find his rhythm. The 2024 NBA Finals MVP picked up 2 fouls in the first quarter and his 4th early in the third, finishing with a quiet 13 points on 4-for-9 shooting (44.4%) while logging a game-worst minus-27 plus-minus. Tatum added 21 points for Boston, while Tyrese Maxey led the 76ers with 24. I still got a lot left in the tank.” “The true revenge game today. JB didn’t show up,” one fan reacted. Another relished the lopsided result, adding, “Revenge never tasted so good.” George, however, played down that idea. item.title: Blázquez double from Rioja assists seals Valencia’s 6-0 Copa del Rey win over Tavernes
item.description: Blázquez double from Rioja assists seals Valencia’s 6-0 Copa del Rey win over Tavernes Aimar Blázquez scored twice from Rioja assists as Valencia beat Tavernes 6-0 at Mestalla, where the hosts were officially the away side. The win follows a 0-3 defeat to Real Madrid and takes Valencia into the second round. Valencia cruised past Tavernes in the Copa del Rey on Tuesday 10 November 2026. The tie was played at the Estadio de Mestalla, yet Valencia were officially the away side in their own stadium. The RFEF had granted Tavernes’ request to stage the match there. Valencia were four goals up inside 23 minutes Raba opened the scoring in the first minute, with Blázquez providing the assist. Raba then turned provider for Duro in the 11th minute. Rioja added the third in the 19th minute after a pass from Martinez. A fourth goal arrived through Elliott in the 23rd minute. Tavernes goalkeeper Mainar kept the margin there three minutes into the second half. He saved a header from Blázquez, who had been set up by Raba. The number 37 struck in the 57th minute and again in the 69th. Danjuma replaced him after 70 minutes, when Gayà also came on for Rioja. Three players were booked. Ugrinic was cautioned in the ninth minute and Montilla of Tavernes in the 22nd. Rioja picked up a yellow card in the 49th minute. Tavernes came closest to a goal when Erik struck the post after a short corner. EFE described the visitors as a sixth-tier club and reported that close to 40 coaches carried their fans to Mestalla. Their municipal ground was not fit for the tie. Mestalla is in its final season before the move to Nou Mestalla. The original 9pm kick-off fell to the RFEF’s postponements A 9pm start had been planned for the tie. Every Copa del Rey match scheduled for that day was called off by the RFEF, and this one was among them. Tavernes reached the first round through the two-legged preliminary round against UD Maracena. The first leg was played at the CD Maracena ground on Sunday 27 September 2026. The two sides drew 1-1 and 0-0. For Valencia, the Real Madrid loss had itself followed a 1-0 win over Elche and a 1-2 defeat to Villarreal. Javier Aguirre said he took positive conclusions from the tie. He welcomed the return of players who had been out long-term. He also said Valencia now need to win in the league. The cup calendar continues with the round of 32 on 16 December. The last 16 follows on 6 January and the quarter-finals on 13 January. The semi-finals are the only two-legged round, with first legs on 10 February and second legs on 3 March. The competition runs until 24 April 2027. Valencia return to league action away to Rayo Vallecano at the Estadio de Vallecas on Saturday 21 November. item.title: Australia used sandpaper even before 2018? Former Aussie spinner Stuart Macgill reveals how he used to rough up balls during matches
item.description: Australia used sandpaper even before 2018? Former Aussie spinner Stuart Macgill reveals how he used to rough up balls during matches originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Former Aussie spinner Stuart MacGill has opened up about some surprising tricks from his playing days. Sandpaper on his thumb helped him change the condition of the ball. His comments raise fresh questions about how new the 2018 Cape Town scandal really was. MORE: Khawaja autobiography highlights: All major talking points from 'Sabr' 'Scratched the daylights out of it!': Stuart MacGill drops shocking sandpaper confession Was sandpaper part of Australian cricket long before the 2018 Cape Town scandal shocked the sporting world? Former Test spinner Stuart MacGill has now offered his own account of life on the field in an earlier era, and it makes for rather uncomfortable reading for those who believed the issue began and ended with one infamous afternoon. MacGill played 44 Tests for Australia between 1998 and 2008, picking up 208 wickets at an average of 29.02. He was widely regarded as one of the most prolific strike bowlers of his generation, and his career ran alongside that of the great Shane Warne. The incidents he described belong to the late 1990s and 2000s, which is well before the March 2018 episode in Cape Town that led to 12-month bans for Steve Smith and David Warner and a nine-month ban for Cameron Bancroft. MORE: Steyn spots irony in Khawaja's Sandpapergate revelation as Broad joins in mocking AUS Stuart MacGill sandpaper admission: How he scratched the ball on his thumb The host got straight to the point and asked whether MacGill had ever used sandpaper. The former leg-spinner did not hesitate, and he went on to explain a clever routine that relied on a small habit of the umpires. During breaks, the match ball would be placed roughly 20 metres beyond the boundary rope, and a fielder would run out to collect it before play resumed. MORE: Usman Khawaja reveals why he waited until retirement to expose Sandpapergate MacGill saw an opportunity in that short run. He fixed a small square of sandpaper to his thumb, picked up the ball after the tea interval, roughed it up and then ripped the paper off before dropping it into the gutter. By the time the first delivery of the session was bowled, no trace of the paper remained. “I’ve used it. What they would do is the umpires, as you’re walking out on the ground, they used to put the ball, sort of about 20 metres over the boundary and leave it there, and you’d run out onto the field, pick it up and go on the field," MacGill said on the Fanatics ​​​​​​podcast. “I taped a little square of sandpaper on my thumb, picked the ball up just after tea, scratched the living daylights out of it, pulled the sandpaper off, chucked it in the gutter before a ball had even been bowled. item.content:encoded: Australia used sandpaper even before 2018? Former Aussie spinner Stuart Macgill reveals how he used to rough up balls during matches originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Former Aussie spinner Stuart MacGill has opened up about some surprising tricks from his playing days. Sandpaper on his thumb helped him change the condition of the ball. His comments raise fresh questions about how new the 2018 Cape Town scandal really was. MORE: Khawaja autobiography highlights: All major talking points from 'Sabr' 'Scratched the daylights out of it!': Stuart MacGill drops shocking sandpaper confession Was sandpaper part of Australian cricket long before the 2018 Cape Town scandal shocked the sporting world? Former Test spinner Stuart MacGill has now offered his own account of life on the field in an earlier era, and it makes for rather uncomfortable reading for those who believed the issue began and ended with one infamous afternoon. MacGill played 44 Tests for Australia between 1998 and 2008, picking up 208 wickets at an average of 29.02. He was widely regarded as one of the most prolific strike bowlers of his generation, and his career ran alongside that of the great Shane Warne. The incidents he described belong to the late 1990s and 2000s, which is well before the March 2018 episode in Cape Town that led to 12-month bans for Steve Smith and David Warner and a nine-month ban for Cameron Bancroft. MORE: Steyn spots irony in Khawaja's Sandpapergate revelation as Broad joins in mocking AUS Stuart MacGill sandpaper admission: How he scratched the ball on his thumb The host got straight to the point and asked whether MacGill had ever used sandpaper. The former leg-spinner did not hesitate, and he went on to explain a clever routine that relied on a small habit of the umpires. During breaks, the match ball would be placed roughly 20 metres beyond the boundary rope, and a fielder would run out to collect it before play resumed. MORE: Usman Khawaja reveals why he waited until retirement to expose Sandpapergate MacGill saw an opportunity in that short run. He fixed a small square of sandpaper to his thumb, picked up the ball after the tea interval, roughed it up and then ripped the paper off before dropping it into the gutter. By the time the first delivery of the session was bowled, no trace of the paper remained. “I’ve used it. What they would do is the umpires, as you’re walking out on the ground, they used to put the ball, sort of about 20 metres over the boundary and leave it there, and you’d run out onto the field, pick it up and go on the field," MacGill said on the Fanatics ​​​​​​podcast. “I taped a little square of sandpaper on my thumb, picked the ball up just after tea, scratched the living daylights out of it, pulled the sandpaper off, chucked it in the gutter before a ball had even been bowled. So nobody even knew that I’d done it, apart from all the scratches on the ball!” Not every experiment went to plan, however. MacGill admitted that he tried a few other ideas as well, including one that ended in a rather funny failure. “I also tried a couple of other things. I sewed a piece of sandpaper inside my trousers one time, but unfortunately that got a hole in my strides, so...” he said. MORE: 'Haven’t paid much attention': Starc denies Khawaja's allegation The SCG Swans race trick: How a full toss helped roughen the ball for reverse swing The third story took place at the Sydney Cricket Ground, where MacGill usually bowled from the Paddington End. He explained that a waist-high full toss was a deliberate tactic because it invited the batter to hook or pull the ball in the direction of the Swans race, the tunnel gate at the ground. Whenever the ball ended up there, the fielder who went to collect it would drag it along the wall on his way back, and that scraping could rough up one side of it to help reverse swing. The mark left behind was clearly visible to anyone who looked closely. “I used to bowl from the Paddington end. If I bowled a waist-high full toss, it was an opportunity for the batsman just to swing me straight down the Swans race. On the occasion that the ball did actually go down there, the fieldsman would walk back up scraping the ball against the wall. There was a big red stripe on the wall!” he said. At one point the host teased MacGill with a quip about a fielder wandering around at deep backward square, and the answer opened up the bigger debate. MacGill brought up Darren Lehmann, the former teammate who later became Australia’s coach, and said he believes that the practice has been around since the earliest days of Test cricket. “You know, Boof (Lehmann) reckons it’s been happening since day one in Test cricket, and I think it probably has been. Because we know that everybody’s doing it, it doesn’t feel so bad. Like if I’m playing against South Africa, I know that they’ve done everything that I’ve done, so I don’t feel bad about it,” he said. In 2018, Cricket Australia presented the sandpaper incident as an unprecedented act devised by Warner and Bancroft, but MacGill’s story points to the use of sandpaper by an Australian player almost two decades earlier, at least in his own case. It also lines up with recent remarks from Usman Khawaja, who claimed in his autobiography Sabr that manipulating the ball was routine in the Sheffield Shield and that “it was all of us” in 2018. Stuart Broad's father, Chris Broad and David Warner have also recently been critical of Lehmann’s public stance of innocence, which makes the new comments even more relevant. MORE: 'Couldn't agree more': David Warner and Stuart Broad's father call out Darren Lehmann's hypocrisy as Sandpapergate fallout continues MacGill’s confession shows why the ball-tampering debate is far from over MacGill’s story is entertaining on the surface, but it should also make cricket think hard about its own history. A thumb covered in sandpaper, a patch stitched into trousers and a scraped ball in the SCG tunnel are not accidental acts. They were planned ideas, and the former spinner describes them with the ease of someone who thought it was part of the job. The most worrying part is the “everybody’s doing it” argument. It may feel natural inside a dressing room, but it is exactly the kind of thinking that allows small rule-bending to grow into something bigger. If players believe that rivals are doing the same, the line between a tactic and cheating becomes blurry, and that is how a scandal like Cape Town can happen. That said, MacGill deserves some credit for speaking so openly, as most players from his era have stayed quiet. His honesty gives the sport a chance to talk about what really took place, rather than pretend the problem started in 2018 and ended with three bans. The game’s authorities should treat these comments as a prompt for a broader conversation. Clearer rules, stricter monitoring of the ball and a culture that does not excuse shortcuts would do more good than harsh punishments after every new revelation. Honest talk about the past is the only way to protect the future. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees have some major decisions to make this offseason, including potentially parting ways with players who have been with the organization for several seasons. New York has endured back-to-back disappointing playoff performances after reaching the World Series, and changes could be coming to the roster. The Yankees also dealt with several injuries in 2026. Second base and third base are two positions the organization may need to address this winter. “This is where Cashman needs to get creative and swing a surprise blockbuster deal for a third baseman, much like he did with Donaldson (even if that failed to work out). Right now, the Yankees' best options at third are Jose Caballero, who didn't see good results there in 2026, and Anthony Volpe, who is still learning the position and doesn't have the ideal arm strength to handle it," SI's Joe Najarian wrote. Jazz Chisholm Jr. has primarily handled second base over the last couple of seasons, but his future in New York is becoming increasingly uncertain. “As the Yankees look to retool their roster for the 2027 season, there's a massive hole they will need to fill. Second base, manned by Jazz Chisholm Jr. for the last two seasons, will explore free agency and it's likely he will not return to the Bronx," SNY's Phillip Martinez wrote. With Chisholm potentially leaving in free agency, MLB Trade Rumors' Steve Adams believes the Yankees could target Brandon Lowe as a replacement. “There’s never been much doubt about Lowe’s power. He belted 35 homers in 2026 — the second-most of his career and his second straight 30-homer campaign (third in his career). Lowe hit .260/.331/.493 with strong batted-ball metrics (91 mph average exit velocity, 45.6% hard-hit rate, 12.5% barrel rate). Sri Lanka suffered an early collapse, losing Pasindu Sooriyabandara (0) and Dinesh Chandimal (1) inside the first four overs. Lahiru Udara offered resistance with 42 off 52 balls, including seven boundaries, before falling to Saqib Khan in the 17th over. Saqib picked up two wickets, while Mohammad Abbas dismissed Sooriyabandara to leave Sri Lanka struggling at 65/3. Kamindu Mendis and Dhananjaya de Silva steadied the innings with an unbeaten 49-run fourth-wicket partnership. Sri Lanka will resume Day 3 at 114/3, trailing Pakistan by 320 runs with seven wickets remaining. Day 2 Tea: Sri Lanka 42/2; 1st innings - Pakistan 434/9d Pakistan continued to dominate the contest after declaring their first innings at 434/9, with Sri Lanka struggling at 42/2 in 12 overs at tea. Mohammad Abbas and debutant Saqib Khan struck early to leave Sri Lanka two wickets down inside the first four overs. Abbas dismissed Pasindu Sooriyabandara for a duck while Saqib removed Dinesh Chandimal for one with an excellent delivery that produced a leading edge. Lahiru Udara offered some resistance with an unbeaten 29 off 35 balls, including four boundaries, while Kamindu Mendis was unbeaten on eight. Sri Lanka will resume the evening session trailing Pakistan by 392 runs, with eight wickets remaining. Day 2 Lunch: Pakistan 390/6 Good start for Pakistan bowlers as Sri Lanka lose two early wickets. Shakeel missed out on his century by a whisker as he departed for 93 runs. After losing nine wickets, Pakistan finally declared their innings closed at 434. A massive total on board, and it is now up to the bowlers to restrict Sri Lanka to a moderate total. Pakistan have lost just one wicket in the first session on Day 2 as they inch closer towards the 400-run mark. A big total loading for the hosts. Saud Shakeel is batting brilliantly, and he is in his 90s. Match resumes at Rawalpindi. The hosts will hope to build on their quality start and hope to add as many runs as possible. Pakistan vs. Sri Lanka 1st Test, Day 1 Score & Updates DAY 1 STUMPS: Pakistan 277/5 (Shakeel 57*, Ghori 3*) Pakistan ended Day 1 at 277/5 after 67.2 overs. Sri Lanka fought back in the final session, picking up two wickets and conceding 65 runs. Debutant Mohammad Taha scored a fighting 51 off 105 balls before falling to Sonal Dinusha. Saud Shakeel remained unbeaten on 57 off 112 deliveries, finally converting his start into a half-century. Salman Agha contributed 16 before being dismissed by Asitha Fernando. Ghazi Ghori was unbeaten on 3 alongside Saud at stumps. Play was stopped due to bad light, with stumps officially called soon after. Only 67.2 overs were bowled on the opening day, with Sri Lanka also struggling with a poor over rate. AT TEA: Pakistan 214/3 (Taha 41*, Shakeel 24*) Pakistan reached 214/3 at tea on Day 1, adding 75 runs and losing just one wicket in the second session. Babar Azam scored a half-century (50 off 58 balls, including seven fours) before being dismissed by Dilshan Madushanka. Madushanka broke the 70-run partnership between Babar and Mohammad Taha, with Kusal Mendis taking the catch behind the stumps. Debutant Mohammad Taha remained unbeaten on 41 off 96 deliveries. Taha survived a dropped catch at 30, when a powerful shot towards short midwicket was not held by Sooriyabandara. Saud Shakeel was unbeaten on 24 off 67 balls, with the pair adding an unbeaten 57-run partnership. Sri Lanka's pacers bowled with greater discipline and extracted movement from the surface, slowing Pakistan's scoring considerably. AT LUNCH: Pakistan 137/2 (Taha 15*, Babar 31*) Pakistan dominated the opening session and reached 137/2 in 29.6 overs at lunch on Day 1 of the first Test against Sri Lanka. Debutant Tayyab Arif smashed a 46-ball half-century, scoring 57 off 51 deliveries, including nine fours and a six. Azan Awais scored 30 off 50 balls as the opening pair added 86 runs off just 97 deliveries. Sri Lanka fought back with two quick wickets, with Milan Rathnayaka dismissing Awais and Asitha Fernando removing Arif. Babar Azam (31*) and debutant Mohammad Taha (15*) remained unbeaten at lunch, putting together an unbeaten partnership. Sri Lanka's seamers struggled with their lines and lengths despite some early movement from the green-looking surface. Toss result: Sri Lanka won the toss and chose to field first. Pakistan will bat on Day 1. Pre-match: Pakistan come into the two-match Test series after beating Sri Lanka 2-1 in the T20Is and winning the ODI tri-series at home, but their red-ball form has been poor. They lost 3-0 to England in their last Test series and have won only two of their last nine Tests. Babar Azam leads a young Pakistan side without Shan Masood, Noman Ali and Sajid Khan, while Mohammad Rizwan missed out despite a double century in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy. Sri Lanka, under new captain Kusal Mendis, are expected to play an extra spinner in the top seven alongside a three-man pace attack. Sri Lanka are seventh in the WTC standings with one win in six Tests, while defeat here would end Pakistan's hopes of reaching the final. Pakistan lead the head-to-head 23-17 from 59 Tests, and the pitch in Rawalpindi is expected to be flat, especially in the first two days. (Photo by Altan Gocher / Hans Lucas / AFP via Getty Images) Getty The Cleveland Cavaliers head coach is under mounting pressure to deliver amid the team’s early-season struggles. Cavaliers head coach Kenny Atkinson is facing growing scrutiny and mounting job pressure amid a disappointing 5-6 start to the 2026-2027 NBA season. Kenny Atkinson’s Future With The Cavaliers In Question Getty CLEVELAND, OHIO – NOVEMBER 02: Head coach Kenny Atkinson of the Cleveland Cavaliers reacts during the third quarter against the Oklahoma City Thunder at Rocket Arena on November 02, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. The Thunder defeated the Cavaliers 117-112. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) On SiriusXM NBA Radio, NBA insider Marc Stein highlighted that Atkinson’s future is a situation to watch closely following the team’s sluggish progress and the lingering questions from their rough Eastern Conference Finals exit. “It’s been a long time since the Cavs got to the Conference Finals without LeBron James on their roster,” Stein said. “But the Conference Finals against the Knicks were so bad that the questions started there. The Cavs decided to back Kenny Atkinson then. But yeah, I mean, it has been a very worrisome start to the season, and I think we have to keep a very close eye on this.” "I think we have to keep a very close eye on this" @TheSteinLine talks to @BGeltzNBA about the Cavs early season struggles Hear Deals and Dunks weekdays at 1 PM ET https://t.co/uGOfTUanJR pic.twitter.com/jFEoVRxAv8 — SiriusXM NBA Radio (@SiriusXMNBA) November 10, 2026 Atkinson notably guided the Cavaliers to a franchise-record 64-win season in his debut 2024-2025 year, but championship-or-bust expectations in Cleveland have shortened the leash following recent slow starts and high-profile meltdowns. Cavaliers’ 5-6 start to the 2026-2027 NBA season stems largely from defensive lapses, starting lineup chemistry issues, and early-season injuries. After reaching the Eastern Conference Finals a year ago, Cleveland entered the campaign with high expectations, yet they have dropped four of their last five games, including a 124-112 loss to an injury-depleted Charlotte Hornets squad. A major driver of the slump is the sharp decline of 37-year-old guard James Harden , who is averaging a career-low 36.4% from the field and 15.3 points per game while drawing heavy criticism for a lack of defensive effort. Compounding these on-court issues is a wave of early injuries and inconsistent rotation management. Key contributors such as Jarrett Allen, Peyton Watson, Sam Merrill , and Jaylon Tyson have missed time. NBA Analyst Kevin O’Connor Believes Roster Is A Bigger Problem Than The Cavaliers Coach Getty Head coach Kenny Atkinson of the Cleveland Cavaliers during the NBA and FIBA’s Basketball Without Borders Next Up 2026 event at Basketball Development Centre in Istanbul, Turkey on August 29, 2026. (Photo by Altan Gocher / Hans Lucas / AFP via Getty Images) NBA analyst Kevin O’Connor believes the Cavaliers’ underwhelming start to the season stems primarily from flawed roster construction rather than head coach Kenny Atkinson. For O’Connor, a coaching change will not solve the team’s deeper personnel issues. He specifically pointed out that the backcourt pairing of Donovan Mitchell and James Harden is an awkward fit, largely because Harden “looks old,” is struggling to finish at the rim, and appears close to falling off a cliff. “I don’t think Cleveland is going to keep Kenny Atkinson all year long. I don’t think the coaching is necessarily the problem. It’s a problem, but not the problem,” O’Connor said. “James Harden looks old. It’s just the reality of it now.” “This Cleveland team just feels flawed to me, with the top four. Mitchell and Harden is an imperfect backcourt. Mobley and Allen is an imperfect frontcourt, and then a bench that I don’t really think is that good,” he added. The Cavaliers, nonetheless, still have a long season ahead to turn things around and reach the same heights they did last season. However, they must decide now if a change is necessary or continue on with what they are trying to build this early in the season. item.title: Duke’s Jon Scheyer gives Michigan State its flowers after close loss
item.description: David Banks-Imagn Images Duke’s Jon Scheyer gives Michigan State its flowers after close loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Duke struggled against Michigan State’s swarming defense on Tuesday , absorbing a tough loss, 79-73, in the State Farm Champions Classic at United Center in Chicago. The No. 2 Blue Devils suffered their first loss , while the No. 5 Spartans remained undefeated in three games. Duke also bowed to Michigan State for the first time in five meetings in the annual tournament. The Spartans held the Blue Devils to just 33.3% shooting, including 7-of-29 from beyond the arc. Duke gave up 16 points on 13 turnovers. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In the postgame conference, Blue Devils coach Jon Scheyer tipped his hat to the Spartans, touting their readiness and cohesion. “Congrats to Michigan State. They 100% deserved to win. I thought they outcompeted us. They played more together. (Jeremy) Fears controlled the whole game. I thought the difference was their role players. They were incredible. (Cam) Ward, what he did in the first half changed the game,” said Scheyer in the video posted by Carolina Blitz. Jon Scheyer’s opening statement after Duke’s 79-73 loss to Michigan State. pic.twitter.com/W9c6Fj5VJQ — Carolina Blitz (@KeepBlitzin) November 11, 2026 Fears had 18 points, seven rebounds, and 11 assists, while Ward added 14 points and six rebounds in 20 minutes off the bench. John Blackwell led Duke with 17 points and five rebounds. He went 5-of-16 from the field. Patrick Ngongba II added 11 points, seven rebounds, six assists, and four blocks. Scheyer pointed out Duke’s lack of synergy and vowed to play better. “For me, it was a little out-of-body experience. I thought we were not connected. That’s just the bottom line. We’re gonna fix it. I can promise you that much. Our fans deserved better. That was not a good performance tonight,” added Scheyer. Duke will try to bounce back against SIU Edwardsville on Friday. Related: Michigan State ends Duke’s 79-game streak with gritty win in State Farm Champions Classic Related: Arizona’s Bryce James goes vertical for epic block vs. Northern Arizona

item.title: From Jersey to Somalia... via Liverpool & Man City
item.description: Somalia midfielder Jarma Mohamed moved to eighth-tier Jersey Bulls in the summer [Lauren Queree/Jersey Bulls] Not many 21-year-olds can say they have played international football, had spells at Liverpool and Manchester City and are now playing in non-league after being spotted on a mobile app. But Jarma Mohamed's footballing journey is not that of your typical midfielder. The combative playmaker has been recalled to Somalia's side for their Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers with Ghana this month, capping a rollercoaster year for the Liverpudlian. "My mum was probably fed up with me just booting stuff in the house, so she got me involved as early as I could," Mohamed jokes with BBC Sport as he talks about the start of his footballing journey. "When I was three she was begging teams to take me because the age that you're allowed is four. "Eventually someone saw me playing and it turned out to be an Everton scout, so I ended up playing for Everton from four and then at that age between four to nine you can play for a few teams. "It was at Liverpool and Everton, eventually chose Liverpool at nine, then signed for Man City at 11. item.content:encoded: Somalia midfielder Jarma Mohamed moved to eighth-tier Jersey Bulls in the summer [Lauren Queree/Jersey Bulls] Not many 21-year-olds can say they have played international football, had spells at Liverpool and Manchester City and are now playing in non-league after being spotted on a mobile app. But Jarma Mohamed's footballing journey is not that of your typical midfielder. The combative playmaker has been recalled to Somalia's side for their Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers with Ghana this month, capping a rollercoaster year for the Liverpudlian. "My mum was probably fed up with me just booting stuff in the house, so she got me involved as early as I could," Mohamed jokes with BBC Sport as he talks about the start of his footballing journey. "When I was three she was begging teams to take me because the age that you're allowed is four. "Eventually someone saw me playing and it turned out to be an Everton scout, so I ended up playing for Everton from four and then at that age between four to nine you can play for a few teams. "It was at Liverpool and Everton, eventually chose Liverpool at nine, then signed for Man City at 11. "I came out of Man City and got a scholarship at Wigan, which is one of the best memories of playing football, having a two-year deal, playing day-in, day-out, full-time schedule, staying in digs up in Wigan, travelling up and down the country for away games, performing, picking up the armband a few times, FA Youth Cup, things like that." Jersey Bulls' midfielder Mohamed wins historic call-up Jersey Bulls sign Somalia midfielder Mohamed Mohamed featured alongside players including Jayden Danns at Liverpool and England stars Rico Lewis and Nico O'Reilly at Manchester City. He was released by Wigan in 2024 and spent time in non-league football with Bamber Bridge and Newcastle Town. His career came to a crossroads in the summer, when Isthmian League South central side Jersey Bulls spotted him on an app for footballers. "I was thinking what do I want to do?," he said. "I could go abroad and do something, but I wasn't really too sure and I'd been playing showcase games with a company called Player, who basically put players in front of teams, they have an app, which is like a LinkedIn for footballers. "Jersey Bulls were on the app looking for players and, long story short, the owner of Player put me in contact with Jersey Bulls. "I know the club's amateur and no-one gets paid, but we worked out a job that aligns with the things that I do, obviously me having Uefa C licence coaching is something that I'd easily do and I've come over and done it." 'Everyone's really together' Jarma Mohamed and his Jersey Bulls team-mates have yet to lose a league game this season [BBC] Mohamed now works as a youth coach in the island, while also anchoring the midfield of a Jersey Bulls side riding high in the eighth tier of English football. Born in Toxteth, Mohamed's Somalian grandfather moved to Liverpool, part of a large Somali community in the city. It is that heritage that has allowed him to play for a side ranked 200th in the world - the lowest of any team to progress to Afcon's final round of qualifiers. He made his Somalia debut against Mauritius in March as the Ocean Stars reached the final qualifying stages for Afcon for the first time in their history - they beat the island nation on penalties after two goalless draws. "It was a random Wednesday afternoon in my kitchen and I was made up," Mohamed says of the moment he was asked to first join the Somalia squad earlier this year. "I could physically see the community close to home, and going out to the camp and experiencing what that's like, it really lit a fire that I didn't even know I could get as far as trying to push my football career." He is part of a Somali squad made up of more players from the global diaspora than those born in the country itself. Having reached the qualifying stage for next summer's tournament, the lowest ranked side left face a tough group against three-time champions Ivory Coast, Gambia and Ghana - who have won the tournament four times and drew 0-0 with England in the group stage of this summer's World Cup. "Everyone's from different parts of the world, you have lads who are Dutch, from Finland, Italy, there's another scouse with me in the team," Mohamed said. "When we're all there, and even lads who are local and playing in the Somali league, everyone's just one family. "That's one thing which we're really good at, we're together as a team, there's no egos. "Everyone's just really together and wanting to get results for the country, which I feel is very important." 'You can only play what's in front of you' Somalia were narrowly beaten by the Ivory Coast in September [Getty Images] In their first two qualifying matches Somalia have not let themselves down. Gambia scored an 83rd-minute winner to overcome them in their opening game, while an Ivory Coast side boasting Real Madrid's summer signing Yan Diomande, Atalanta's Franck Kessie and former Arsenal winger Nicolas Pepe scored in the 89th minute and the fifth minute added time to earn a 2-0 win. It means the Somalis are second-from-bottom of their group on goal difference from a Ghana side managed by former Real Madrid boss Carlos Queiroz who have lost their opening two matches. With the tense security situation in Somalia the Ocean Stars have played all their qualifiers away from home and will face Ghana in their back-to-back matches in Accra. So how will Mohamed, who plays in front of sparse crowds in small grounds in the area south of London, approach facing opponents who ply their trade in the biggest leagues in the world? "The same way I treat every game, you can only play what's in front of you," he added. "If you play the name or an occasion you're losing before you've even kicked a ball. "I just play who's in front of me and keep it at that. "You know the players' levels, the qualities that they have that you have to respect, but you also have to back yourself. "You're sharing the same pitch for a reason, it's not by accident." And can the Ocean Stars make next summer's tournament in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania? "The aim is to qualify," he added. "If you come to do nothing less than that you may as well stay home. "In the two games we've had previously against Ivory Coast and Gambia we've shown that we can compete. "If you come to play for the experience or 'we're just happy to be there', then there's no point in coming. "We need to come to try and win." Related internet links Jersey Bulls

item.title: National Champion QB Drops Bold Theory Behind Indiana’s Sudden Drop in Rankings
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 12: Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti looks up during the second half against the Howard Bison at Memorial Stadium on September 12, 2026 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) Getty The Indiana Hoosiers trended for all the wrong reasons Tuesday night. Fans and analysts started believing IU became punished for taking a bye, dropping five spots in the College Football Playoff rankings. Many chimed in, but Danny Kanell believes there’s a deeper theory. The 1993 national champion quarterback for Florida State dropped his bold take following the ranking reveal. The now CBS Sports analyst has reason to believe Curt Cignetti’s past words may have played a role here. “Indiana drops 5 spots on a BYE week. Looks like that committee didn’t appreciate Curt Cignetti’s comments this week,” Kanell posted on the social media website X, formerly known as Twitter. Looks like it’s time to revisit those Cignetti words. Tracing Back to Curt Cignetti’s CFP Rip Cignetti called out a bias the College Football Playoff committee shows toward the SEC. All during a November press conference before the Hoosiers had their bye. “SEC gets a lot of love from ESPN and all their writers that they don’t technically pay but march to their drum,” Cignetti ranted toward reporters. “And that’s why you see all these SEC teams up there and some good two-loss teams from the Big Ten not quite as high.” Cignetti ended with: “But like I said, it’s all gonna play out on the field.” Indiana did just that last year in breezing through 16-0 overall. That included toppling longtime SEC heavyweight Alabama with a 38-3 rout in the Rose Bowl. IU then took down two more heavyweights from outside the SEC: Oregon in the Peach Bowl (56-22) then Miami for the national championship (27-21). But now Kanell believes that Cignetti rant likely doomed his team when the committee formed the newest rankings. Other Theories Sprout Behind Indiana’s Drop Kanell isn’t the only national college football media personality who reacted to the stunning drop. College football insider for On3/Rivals Brett McMurphy called out another aspect attached to IU. “Indiana doesn’t need to worry about dropping five spots to No. 9. The Hoosiers have their non-conference schedule to boost their resume,” McMurphy posted on X. Richard Johnson of CBS Sports became more relentless toward Indiana. “Indiana, it’s simple! If you don’t like that seed that you’re in right now, go beat a ranked USC team!” Johnson said during a broadcast. "Indiana, it's simple! item.title: William Nylander ‘Can Play Better,’ Says Maple Leafs HC Jim Hiller
item.description: William Nylander Jim Hiller Maple Leafs Getty Toronto Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller said that star forward William Nylander “can play better” after the team lost yet again. The Maple Leafs lost 6-3 to the Colorado Avalanche on Tuesday night for their fourth straight defeat, dropping the team to 8-10-2 on the season through their first 20 games. Nylander was held off the scoresheet while also being a -4 for the team, by far the worst +/- of any player on the ice for the Maple Leafs. After the game, the team’s head coach said that his star winger needs to be better. William Nylander Struggling for Maple Leafs Speaking to reporters following the Maple Leafs’ 6-3 loss to the Avalanche on Tuesday, Hiller said that he wants Nylander to play better, and he believes that the player feels the same way about his play. “I know he can play better than he is right now. I think that’s a pretty fair statement. If you asked him, I think he’d agree,” Hiller said. Jim Hiller on William Nylander: “I know he can play better than he is right now. I think that’s a pretty fair statement. If you asked him, I think he’d agree.” @sdpnsports — Jesse Blake (@JesseBlake) November 11, 2026 Maple Leafs Need More From Star Winger The Maple Leafs have lost four straight games, and in those four losses, Nylander has scored just 1 goal with 0 assists. Given that he is one of the team’s highest-paid players at $11.5 million, he absolutely needs to produce, or else the team will be in trouble keeping pace, scoring-wise, with other teams. This season, Nylander has 11 goals and 11 assists for 22 points, so overall he’s had a decent season scoring-wise. But with the Maple Leafs really struggling right now during the team’s current losing skid, Nylander’s struggles are really starting to stand out, and that’s why Hiller called on him to pick up his play, as Toronto needs him to light the lamp, especially with fellow star winger Kirill Marchenko currently out of the team’s lineup with an injury. That being said, Nylander is far from the only Maple Leafs player who is struggling to score right now, so these losses are not all on him. But when you have one of the highest cap hits on the team, you need to score, or else the team is going to struggle to win games. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post William Nylander ‘Can Play Better,’ Says Maple Leafs HC Jim Hiller appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Celtics star Jayson Tatum opens up on making LeBron James his first poster victim since injury
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Celtics star Jayson Tatum opens up on making LeBron James his first poster victim since injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jayson Tatum turned back the clock against the Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday night, and the Boston Celtics star admitted that his poster dunk on LeBron James meant more to him than just two points . Midway through the third quarter, Tatum split a double team, drove hard to the rim and threw down a one-handed slam right over James . After the game, Tatum explained why the play felt so special. “It just kind of felt good to finish through contact. It’s been about 19 months since I dunked on somebody. Just to kind of get my legs back, feeling good, it’s a basketball play,” the 28-year-old said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Jayson Tatum on dunking on LeBron James : "It just kind of felt good to finish through contact. It's been about 19 months since I dunked on somebody. Just to kind of get my legs back, feeling good, it's a basketball play" pic.twitter.com/wlsIgAtwVY — Oh No He Didn't 🤯 (@ohnohedidnt24) November 11, 2026 That stretch without a poster dunk speaks to the long road Tatum has traveled. The six-time All-Star tore his right Achilles tendon during the second round of the 2025 playoffs, an injury that sidelined him for much of the 2025-26 season . He finally made his return on March 6 against the Dallas Mavericks. Ahead of that return, ESPN’s Shams Charania reported that the mental side of regaining confidence in his leg was the biggest hurdle for Tatum , which makes his comments about getting his legs back all the more meaningful. Now, Tatum looks like he is regaining his explosiveness. The dunk also brought back memories of one of the most iconic moments of his career, when he posterized James as a rookie in Game 7 of the 2018 Eastern Conference Finals . That one came in a losing effort, but this time, Tatum and the Celtics came out on top. Boston cruised to a 123-101 win over Philadelphia. Tatum finished with 21 points on 8-of-17 shooting, along with six rebounds, four assists and two blocks. Paul George led the way with 36 points against his former team , while Payton Pritchard chipped in 18. The win carried extra meaning, as it was Tatum’s first matchup against Jaylen Brown since his longtime teammate was traded to the Sixers. The victory improved Boston to 9-2 on the season. Next up is a road date with the Toronto Raptors on Wednesday. Related: Kevin O’Connor explains why Paul George is ‘better fit’ for Jayson Tatum than Jaylen Brown Related: 76ers’ Joel Embiid calls Paul George Celtics’ ‘best player’

item.title: Padres Sign Right-Handed Starter in First Offseason Move of 2026
item.description: Apr 25, 2024; Denver, Colorado, USA; Detailed view of the cap and glove of pitcher Randy Vásquez (98) (not pictured) in seventh inning against the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field.
